lineages.title: Men in Black
lineages.creator: Lowell Cunningham

divergence.label: First contact and the neutral zone
divergence.delta: Real: unidentified flying objects stay unidentified and the government denies everything. Fiction: a handful of agents make first contact with alien refugees, declare Earth a neutral zone, and build a uniformed bureaucracy to police the aliens already living among us.
divergence.note: 1961 is the franchise's founding date for the agency's public-facing mission; the films anchor the era through the young Agent K and the 1960s timeline of the third film rather than through a stated calendar year.

ending.why: Every threat is contained, Earth stays protected and ignorant, and the branch that was exposed is quietly rebuilt.

events.title: The agency is founded in secret
events.description: A small group of government agents forms the Men in Black to monitor alien activity on Earth, an agency with no congressional oversight, no public record and a monopoly on the memory-wiping technology that keeps it invisible.
events.note: The agency's creation is placed in the late 1950s by franchise tie-in material; the films themselves only establish that it predates the 1961 first contact and the 1969 events.
events.binWhy: A body is founded that will shape everything after it.

facets.change: no oversight → an agency founded in secret

events.title: First contact with the refugees
events.description: Agents including the young K meet a group of alien refugees, and Earth is declared a neutral zone for extraterrestrials, turning a one-off encounter into a standing diplomatic policy that the public never hears about.
events.note: The founding year of the agency's mission is fixed by franchise reference rather than stated on screen in the 1997 film.
events.binWhy: A non-human intelligence is confirmed, met or intervenes.

facets.change: a chance meeting → the planet declared a neutral zone

events.title: Alien spacecraft open as the World's Fair
events.description: The Unisphere and the observation towers built for the New York World's Fair are functioning alien structures hidden in plain sight, the template for the agency's habit of disguising its hardware as human landmarks.
events.note: Established in franchise tie-in material and revisited in the films, where the 1964 fairground site is where the first film's climax takes place.
events.binWhy: Alien hardware hidden in plain sight as landmarks.

facets.change: alien hardware → hidden in plain sight as landmarks

events.title: The ArcNet launched under Apollo 11
events.description: Agent K defeats the Boglodite assassin Boris the Animal at Cape Canaveral and launches the ArcNet shield on the Apollo 11 launch night, a planetary defence system the public reads as a moon rocket.
events.note: The third film stages this on the real Apollo 11 launch date of 16 July 1969 and calls it the fixed point on which humanity's survival depends.
events.binWhy: A planetary defence system launched under the cover of a Moon rocket.

facets.change: planet undefended → a shield launched under cover of a moon rocket

events.title: Agent J is recruited
events.description: NYPD officer James Darrell Edwards III chases a Cephalapoid through Manhattan, is recruited into the Men in Black and helps stop the Bug from stealing the Galaxy, while the public sees only a routine crime wave.
events.note: The first film's release year is also its story year, keeping the franchise's present identical to the audience's.
events.binWhy: An ordinary person is drawn into the larger story.

facets.change: a police officer → recruited into the agency that does not exist

events.title: The Light of Zartha
events.description: The Kylothian queen Serleena takes over the New York headquarters in her search for the Light of Zartha, forcing J to restore K's memory and revealing that an alien royal has been living quietly on Earth for decades.
events.note: The second film is set five years after the first, in its own release year.
events.binWhy: What was hidden is exposed.

facets.change: headquarters → seized by an alien queen; a hidden royal revealed

events.title: Boris the Animal rewrites the moon launch
events.description: Boris escapes LunarMax and travels back to 1969 to kill the young Agent K, briefly erasing K from history and forcing J to restore the timeline in which the ArcNet was launched.
events.note: The film is set in its release year before the time jump, and its 1969 sequence is the same fixed point charted above.
events.binWhy: Someone or something arrives out of its own time and changes the present.

facets.change: the past → an escaped prisoner goes back to kill his captor

events.title: The London branch is exposed
events.description: Molly Wright, who has hunted the Men in Black since a childhood alien encounter, finds the agency on her own and is recruited in London, uncovering a Hive infiltration inside the organisation.
events.note: Set in its release year and noted for giving the franchise its first recruit who was not memory-wiped into the job.
events.binWhy: An ordinary person is drawn into the larger story.

facets.change: a childhood witness → finds the agency herself; an infiltration exposed

lineages.groupingNote: Men in Black runs entirely on concealment: the aliens were always here, the agency was founded in secret, and the public record of the 1960s is left intact while being quietly falsified from the inside. On the real axis it spans 1958 to 2019 — one T4 event for the agency's founding, five T3 events for the 1960s decade the films treat as their origin story, and three T2 events for the beats set in the audience's own century. Its T1 tier is empty because the fiction stops in our near future: for all the galaxy-spanning traffic, no Men in Black story is set more than a few decades past the present, which is exactly what keeps the conceit — they are among us, now, and you have already met one — intact.

lineages.title: The Three-Body Problem
lineages.creator: Liu Cixin (translated by Ken Liu and Joel Martinsen)

divergence.label: Ye Wenjie transmits to the stars from Red Coast
divergence.delta: Real: 1971. China's first satellite had flown the year before, and humanity's first deliberate message to the stars, from Arecibo, was three years away. Fiction: a persecuted astrophysicist at a secret Chinese military base uses the Sun as an amplifier and sends a message that is heard four light years away.
divergence.inUniverse: Red Coast Base, 1971; the reply arrives about eight years later, in October 1979

sources.title: Wikipedia: The Three-Body Problem (novel)
Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table
Wikipedia: Arecibo message (1974)

divergence.note: Everything before 1971 in the novel is real history: the Cultural Revolution, the struggle sessions, the Inner Mongolia production corps. The fork is placed at the transmission, the first act that could not have happened in our world. The year comes from the fan timelines and from the novel's statement that the reply took about eight years; the 1979 reply is dated more firmly.

ending.why: The Solar System has been flattened into two dimensions, humanity survives only as a few scattered colonies, and the book ends with Cheng Xin returning her refuge's mass to a dying universe in the mere hope that it will be reborn.

events.title: Ye Zhetai is beaten to death at a struggle session
events.description: At Tsinghua University, Red Guards beat the physicist Ye Zhetai to death for teaching relativity and the Big Bang, while his daughter Ye Wenjie watches and her mother denounces him. It is the moment Ye Wenjie loses faith in humanity, and every later link in the chain runs back to it.

sources.title: Wikipedia: The Three-Body Problem (novel)
Wikipedia: Cultural Revolution

events.note: The Cultural Revolution and its struggle sessions at Tsinghua are real history; Ye Zhetai is fictional. The novel opens in 1967, and the English edition restored the Cultural Revolution chapters to the front of the book.
events.binWhy: A movement sanctioned by the state kills a scientist for his physics; it is an attack on a group (intellectuals), not a war or a seizure of power.

facets.change: a physicist teaching relativity → dead on a stage, his daughter watching

events.title: Ye Wenjie uses the Sun to send a message to the stars
events.description: At Red Coast, a secret military base on Radar Peak, Ye Wenjie aims the transmitter at the Sun, which she has worked out will amplify radio waves at certain frequencies, and so broadcasts a message about Earth into the galaxy. Nobody at the base knows that the message has been sent.
events.inUniverse: Red Coast transmission, 1971 (roughly eight years before the 1979 reply)

sources.title: Wikipedia: The Three-Body Problem (novel)
Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table

events.note: Wikipedia's summary has the reply arriving about eight years after her broadcast, and the fan timelines put the transmission in 1971, which gives 1979. The real first deliberate interstellar message, from Arecibo, was three years later in 1974 and did not use the Sun as an amplifier.
events.binWhy: A transmitter is used in a way nobody had tried before, amplified by the Sun; what changes is that Earth can now be heard, and the reply comes later as a separate event.

facets.change: a planet nobody could hear → one that has broadcast its presence

events.title: Ye Wenjie answers Trisolaris
events.description: A pacifist Trisolaran listener picks up the message and sends back a warning: do not answer, or your world will be invaded. Ye Wenjie answers anyway and invites them, then kills her husband and the political commissar who could have found the message. On Trisolaris the reply fixes Earth's location, and a fleet is sent on a journey of more than four hundred years.
events.inUniverse: October 1979, Red Coast Base

sources.title: Wikipedia: The Three-Body Problem (novel)
Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table
Douban review: 《三体》三部曲历史年表 (fan chronology; flags the 201X vs 2007 Crisis Era contradiction)

events.note: Both the Fandom timeline and the Douban chronology give October 21, 1979. Trisolaris is about four light years away, which is why the round trip took about eight years. In our 1979 nothing has ever answered a signal from Earth.
events.binWhy: Humanity, through one person, is contacted by a non-human intelligence and answers it.

facets.change: a warning not to answer → an invitation to invade

events.title: The Earth-Trisolaris Organization is founded
events.description: Ye Wenjie and the American oil heir Mike Evans, who has given up on humanity, found an organisation to help the Trisolarans conquer Earth, with the ship Judgment Day as its base and the second Red Coast station aboard. Its members, many of them scientists, recruit through a virtual-reality game and spend two decades preparing for the fleet.
events.inUniverse: Founding of the ETO at the Second Red Coast Base, 1980s

sources.title: Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Earth-Trisolaris Organization
Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table
Douban review: 《三体》三部曲历史年表 (fan chronology; flags the 201X vs 2007 Crisis Era contradiction)

events.note: The novel says only that the ETO was founded in the 1980s, after Evans received word from Trisolaris. 1988 is the year both the Fandom timeline and the Douban chronology give, but the novel does not state it outright.
events.binWhy: A secret society is founded that shapes the next two decades, and after them the Crisis Era.

facets.change: one woman's secret → an organisation working against its own species

events.title: The Three-Body Problem is serialized in Science Fiction World
events.description: Liu Cixin's novel runs in the Chinese magazine Science Fiction World in 2006 and comes out as a book in 2008. Ken Liu's English translation followed in 2014 and won the 2015 Hugo Award.

sources.title: Wikipedia: The Three-Body Problem (novel)

events.note: Wikipedia dates the serialization to 2006 without giving a month. The English release in 2014 is not a separate event, because a lineage has only one event per year and the 2014 slot in this chain is empty.
events.binWhy: Publication of the original work; it has no bin because it is not a moment in the fiction's history.

events.title: Physics stops working, and the world learns the fleet is coming
events.description: Particle accelerators return impossible results and leading physicists kill themselves. Investigators trace the cause to the ETO and, in Operation Guzheng, slice the Judgment Day apart in the Panama Canal with nanofilament to capture its archive, which shows that proton-sized Trisolaran computers called sophons are sabotaging experiments and watching everything, and that the fleet will arrive in about four centuries. The Crisis Era begins.
events.inUniverse: Year 1 of the Crisis Era (the book's present)

sources.title: Wikipedia: The Three-Body Problem (novel)
Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table
Douban review: 《三体》三部曲历史年表 (fan chronology; flags the 201X vs 2007 Crisis Era contradiction)

events.note: The novel never gives its present a year. Death's End's era table dates the start of the Crisis Era only as '201X'. The fan chronology works back from the characters' ages (Ye Wenjie retired in 2004, Yang Dong was born in 1980) to 2007, which is the year used here. The sophon lockdown, Operation Guzheng and the public announcement all happen in the same short stretch and are merged into one event. In our 2007 the Large Hadron Collider was a year from switching on, and nobody found anything wrong with it.
events.binWhy: What defines the moment is that knowledge the ETO had kept hidden for thirty years is exposed, and the whole world is told.

facets.change: scientists dying over broken results → a world told the invasion is coming

events.title: The UN names four Wallfacers
events.description: Because the sophons can see and hear everything humans do except what they think, the UN Planetary Defense Council gives four men power to carry out strategies they never have to explain. The ETO answers by naming a Wallbreaker for each of them. Luo Ji, an unknown sociologist, is chosen because Trisolaris wants him dead, and in Year 8 he casts a 'spell': he broadcasts the location of a nearby star to test what Ye Wenjie told him about the universe.
events.inUniverse: Crisis Era, Year 3 (Wallfacer Act passed at the 19th PDC session)

sources.title: Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Wallfacer (Wallfacer Act, Crisis Era Year 3)
Wikipedia: The Dark Forest

events.note: The Dark Forest heads the chapter 'Year 3, Crisis Era'. The conversion counts forward from the 2007 used for Year 1. If you count back from Death's End's 2208 instead, you get 2003, which is before the book's own present, so for the early Crisis Era the forward count is used.
events.binWhy: A new body with its own powers is set up by international law, and it shapes the war for two centuries.

facets.change: strategy an enemy can overhear → four men whose plans live only in their heads

events.title: The Staircase Project launches Yun Tianming's brain
events.description: Humanity sends a probe toward the Trisolaran fleet, pushed by a chain of nuclear explosions and carrying only the frozen brain of Yun Tianming, a terminally ill man. A cable fails, and the probe drifts off course and is lost. Two and a half centuries later it turns out the Trisolarans caught it and rebuilt him, and that the fairy tales he later tells hide the secrets of lightspeed travel.
events.inUniverse: Crisis Era, Year 7 (Death's End)

sources.title: Wikipedia: Death's End
Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table

events.note: The Fandom timeline puts the launch and Cheng Xin's hibernation in Crisis Year 7; that converts to 2013 by the same forward count from 2007. Wikipedia places it only in 'the 2010s'. There is another inconsistency: in Deterrence Year 61 (2269) Cheng Xin is said to have been asleep for 264 years, which would put the start of her sleep in 2005.
events.binWhy: A first mission departs for somewhere nobody has reached: the enemy fleet, light years out.

facets.change: no human anywhere near the enemy → a frozen brain sent to meet them

events.title: The Doomsday Battle: one droplet destroys the fleet
events.description: After two centuries of rebuilding, a confident human fleet of about two thousand warships goes out to capture the first Trisolaran probe to arrive, a mirror-smooth droplet made of strong-interaction material. In under an hour it rams through almost all of them, and the few ships that escape into deep space turn on each other for supplies. The same year, astronomers see that the star Luo Ji named has been destroyed, which proves the dark-forest idea.
events.inUniverse: Crisis Era, Year 205

sources.title: Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Doomsday Battle (Crisis Era Year 205)
Wikipedia: The Dark Forest
Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table

events.note: Year 205 is stated in The Dark Forest. Counted back from Death's End's statement that the Crisis Era ended in 2208, with deterrence in Crisis Year 208, it is 2205. The Fandom wiki counts forward instead and gets 2213; the Douban chronology gets 2214. The books' own anchors disagree by about eight years here.
events.binWhy: A single battle decides the military contest: humanity's fleet is annihilated, and that settles that it cannot win by force.

facets.change: a fleet sure of victory → a handful of fugitive ships

events.title: Luo Ji establishes dark-forest deterrence
events.description: At Ye Wenjie's grave, Luo Ji reveals that the nuclear bombs he had placed around the Sun can broadcast Trisolaris's location to the rest of the galaxy, and threatens to set them off if the droplets move against Earth. That would doom both worlds, and Trisolaris backs down. Luo Ji becomes the Swordholder, and a balance of terror between two civilisations begins, with technology flowing to Earth.
events.inUniverse: Crisis Era, Year 208; the Deterrence Era begins

sources.title: Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table

Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Deterrence Era (62 years)

events.note: Death's End's era table dates the start of the Deterrence Era to 2208. That is the firmest anchor in the whole Crisis Era.
events.binWhy: A weapon that could end both civilisations is armed, and the balance of power freezes around it; this is the definition of the bin.

facets.change: a species waiting to be exterminated → a hostage holding its captor hostage

events.title: Deterrence fails within minutes of the handover
events.description: Luo Ji hands the switch to Cheng Xin, chosen by a softer age that no longer trusts hard men. Minutes later droplets attack the broadcast antennas, and she cannot bring herself to press it. Trisolaris takes Earth and orders the whole human population into Australia, where famine and violence kill hundreds of millions.
events.inUniverse: Deterrence Era, Year 62 (the Post-Deterrence Era begins)

events.binWhy: Humanity is disarmed and its territory occupied; people are moved into one continent under the invader's rule.

facets.change: a sixty-two-year balance of terror → a disarmed species herded into Australia

events.title: The Gravity broadcast reveals Trisolaris to the universe
events.description: Far from Earth, the crews of the warships Blue Space and Gravity use four-dimensional space to destroy the droplets chasing them. They then vote to send the gravitational-wave broadcast that Cheng Xin did not. When it is known on Earth, the Trisolarans give up the occupation and leave, ending the internment in Australia, but the broadcast has also marked where the Sun is.
events.inUniverse: Beginning of the Broadcast Era (2272)

events.binWhy: The one thing both worlds had kept hidden, where Trisolaris is, is exposed to everyone who might be listening.

facets.change: coordinates held as a threat → coordinates broadcast to the galaxy

events.title: A photoid destroys the Trisolaran star
events.description: Three years and ten months after the broadcast, an unknown civilisation fires a relativistic particle, a photoid, at one of Trisolaris's suns, and the planet and its world are destroyed. Earth now knows the dark forest is real. It knows its own location was exposed by the same broadcast, and it begins building bunker cities behind the gas giants.
events.inUniverse: Broadcast Era, Year 3 (three years ten months after the broadcast)

sources.title: Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table

events.binWhy: An attack from outside kills an entire civilisation's homeworld, and it changes how humanity lives from then on.

facets.change: a living enemy homeworld → a destroyed star system

events.title: A dual-vector foil flattens the Solar System
events.description: A passing alien, the Singer, sends a scrap of two-dimensional space into the Solar System almost in passing. Over a few days, space collapses into it and everything, the Sun, the planets and the bunker cities built since 2333, is flattened into a picture on a plane. Luo Ji stays behind at a museum on Pluto; Cheng Xin and AA escape on the Halo, the one ship secretly fitted with a lightspeed drive.
events.inUniverse: Bunker Era, Year 67 (end of the Bunker Era)

sources.title: Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table
Wikipedia: Death's End

events.note: Death's End's table ends the Bunker Era in 2400. The Bunker Era begins in 2333, and 2333 plus 67 gives 2400, so the two anchors agree. The Douban fan chronology's 2354 does not match the table.
events.binWhy: An attack kills almost all of humanity at once; nothing in the Solar System is left to rebuild.

facets.change: a system of bunker cities → a painting on a plane

events.title: Cheng Xin gives the mass of her small universe back
events.description: Cheng Xin and Guan Yifan are stranded in the lightspeed-lowered black domain around DX3906 (from 2687). When they come out nearly nineteen million years later, they take shelter in Universe 647, a tiny pocket universe Yun Tianming left for them. A broadcast from the 'Returners' asks every pocket universe to give back its mass so that the main universe can collapse and be reborn, and they go back, leaving behind a bottle of messages and a small ecosystem.
events.inUniverse: Timeline for Universe 647 (begins 18906416, after the Black Domain Era for DX3906, 2687–18906416)

sources.title: Three-Body Problem Wiki (Fandom): Timeline, with the era ranges from Death's End's front-matter table
Wikipedia: Death's End

events.note: Death's End's era table says the Universe 647 timeline begins in 18906416, and that is the year used here. The Returners' call reaches them after a year inside the pocket universe, when an unstated, far greater span has passed in the main universe; the book gives no date for the end of the universe.
events.binWhy: The last jump forward shows what became of everything: the Solar System is long gone, the universe is dying, and one of the last humans decides its fate.

facets.change: a pocket universe to outlast the end → its mass returned to a dying cosmos

lineages.groupingNote: It belongs in hidden-history because the fork is a secret act inside real history. A message sent from a classified Chinese base during the Cultural Revolution is answered, and for three decades the answer is known only to a conspiracy (the ETO) while the world goes on looking like ours. It becomes public only in the book's present. This chain follows Liu Cixin's Chinese novels in their English translations, not the Tencent (2023) or Netflix (2024) adaptations, which move events around. Crisis Era dates are converted two ways because the books disagree with themselves. The start is given as '201X' and the book's present works out to 2007, so early Crisis years are counted forward from 2007. Death's End ends the Crisis Era in 2208 at Year 208, so late Crisis years are counted back from 2208. The Deterrence, Broadcast and Bunker eras follow Death's End's own table. Tiers: T4 is empty because the chain reaches back only to 1967. T3 holds the Cultural Revolution and the Red Coast years. T2 runs from 2006 to 2275. T1 holds the flattening of the Solar System in 2400 and the end of the universe, dated by the book's 18906416.

lineages.title: Fringe
lineages.creator: J. J. Abrams, Alex Kurtzman and Roberto Orci

divergence.label: Bell and Bishop begin the Cortexiphan trials
divergence.delta: Real: 1981 is the year of the IBM PC and the first space shuttle; nobody is dosing three-year-olds in a Florida day-care centre to unlock powers of the mind. Fiction: William Bell and Walter Bishop create the nootropic Cortexiphan and trial it on children in Jacksonville and Ohio, and one of those children, Olivia Dunham, will be able to cross between universes.
divergence.inUniverse: Cortexiphan created by Bell and Bishop in 1981; trials in Jacksonville, Florida, and Ohio
divergence.note: Wikipedia dates Cortexiphan to the early 1980s; the Fringe wiki gives 1981. The series also shows photographs of Observers at the Boston Massacre and Franz Ferdinand's assassination, but by design they change nothing there, so they are not taken as the fork. The first dated act that makes this world stop being ours is the drug trial; the load-bearing act, Walter's 1985 crossing into the parallel universe, follows four years later.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mythology of Fringe (Cortexiphan developed in the early 1980s, testing through 1986)
Fringe Wiki: Cortexiphan (created 1981; trials 1981-1983 in Ohio and Jacksonville)

ending.why: Walter takes the child Michael to 2167 so the Observers are never made; the timeline resets to the day of the 2015 invasion, the invasion does not happen, and Peter, Olivia and their daughter Etta are alive in the park.

events.title: The Cortexiphan trials
events.description: Two scientists give an experimental drug to young children in Jacksonville and Ohio to stop the natural narrowing of the mind. Most of the children forget; a few, including Olivia Dunham, are left with abilities that no one outside the trial knows about.

sources.title: Fringe Wiki: Cortexiphan
Wikipedia: Mythology of Fringe

events.note: The year comes from the fan wiki; Wikipedia says only 'early 1980s'. In the timeline this lineage follows (seasons 4 and 5), Olivia runs away from the trials after six months, but her abilities remain and matter in 2012 and 2036.
events.binWhy: Children are dosed and one of them is chosen, without her knowledge, as the person the future turns on.

facets.change: ordinary children → secret trial subjects with latent powers

events.title: Walter crosses into the other universe
events.description: Walter Bishop, whose son has died of a genetic illness, breaks through to a parallel universe to cure that world's Peter, and on the way back father and son fall through the ice of Reiden Lake. The crossing damages the fabric between the universes, and the other side begins to tear open.
events.inUniverse: In the seasons 4-5 timeline Peter drowns in Reiden Lake; in the seasons 1-3 timeline an Observer saves him and Walter raises him

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mythology of Fringe (the 1985 episode 'Peter'; the weak spot created by Walter in 1985)
Fringe Wiki: Alternate Timeline (1985: Peter drowns in Reiden Lake)

events.note: The episode 'Peter' is set in 1985. Both timelines share the crossing and the damage it does; they differ only in whether the boy survives the lake. The other universe, where the Twin Towers stand and airships are common, is from here on in the story's own politics.
events.binWhy: A passage between universes is made for the first time.

facets.change: two sealed universes → a breach between them

events.title: Flight 627 lands with everyone dead
events.description: An international flight from Hamburg lands at Boston's Logan Airport with every passenger and crew member killed by a flesh-dissolving toxin. The FBI's Fringe Division, working with Walter Bishop, finds the attack was an experiment in a wider series of events it names the Pattern.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Fringe season 1 ('Pilot', aired 9 September 2008)
Fringe Wiki: Alternate Timeline (2008-2010: John Scott dies from his injuries in the Flight 627 investigation)

events.note: The pilot is set in its own present, 2008. The event happens in both timelines. In our 2008 no aircraft landed with everyone aboard dead; the fiction's public record is a string of unexplained disasters the FBI files as terrorism.
events.binWhy: A targeted chemical attack on an airliner, short of war, begins the story.

facets.change: an ordinary flight → an aircraft full of the dead

events.title: The other side sends its agents across
events.description: The parallel universe, which blames ours for the vortices and quarantine zones tearing it apart, sends Olivia's double across to take her place while the real Olivia is held on the other side. The two worlds are now at war in secret, each with its own Fringe Division.
events.inUniverse: Seasons 4-5 timeline: Olivia is held for two weeks, not months as in seasons 2-3

sources.title: Fringe Wiki: Alternate Timeline (Fauxlivia kidnaps Olivia; locked away for two weeks)
Wikipedia: Mythology of Fringe

events.note: The year is derived: the swap is shown at the end of season 2 (May 2010) and through season 3, set in the show's present. The seasons 4-5 timeline keeps the swap but shortens it. None of this is public in our universe; in the other one the damage is public and the amber quarantines are policy.
events.binWhy: Two worlds settle into a covert war of infiltration and sabotage.

facets.change: two universes unaware of each other → a covert war of doubles

events.title: The Bridge between the universes
events.description: A machine left in both universes links them through a room where the two sides can meet, and the war stops. The two Fringe Divisions begin working together to heal the damage, and the two Walters, one of whom stole the other's son, sit at the same table.
events.inUniverse: The seasons 4-5 timeline begins here: Peter enters the machine, makes the Bridge and is erased; he returns later that year

sources.title: Fringe Wiki: Alternate Timeline (2011: the Bridge is formed, cooperation begins)
Wikipedia: Fringe season 4 ('Neither Here Nor There': the two Fringe Divisions working together)

events.note: The Bridge is made at the end of season 3 (May 2011) and season 4 opens with the two divisions a week into cooperating (September 2011). This is the point where the lineage chooses its timeline: from here the chart follows the timeline without Peter, which is the one the series ends in.
events.binWhy: Two enemies at war agree to work together through a shared crossing.

facets.change: a war between universes → a joint task force

events.title: The Bridge is shut and Bell's plan is stopped
events.description: David Robert Jones, working for William Bell, synchronises earthquakes in both universes to collapse them; the two sides switch the Bridge off and separate for good. Bell then tries to destroy this universe to build a new one, and Walter stops him by shooting Olivia, who survives.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Fringe season 4 ('Worlds Apart', 'Brave New World')
Fringe Wiki: Alternate Timeline (2012)

events.note: The finale aired in May 2012 in the show's present. Olivia is pregnant with Etta by the end; the daughter is the reason September let this timeline stand.
events.binWhy: The fight with Bell and Jones is won, and the borders between the universes close.

facets.change: two linked universes under attack → two sealed ones, both intact

events.title: The final episode airs
events.description: Fox broadcasts 'Liberty' and 'An Enemy of Fate', the last two episodes, ending the series after five seasons and a hundred episodes.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Fringe season 5 ('An Enemy of Fate', aired 18 January 2013)

events.note: The series premiered on 9 September 2008, but 2008 is taken by the Flight 627 event and the lineage allows one entry per year, so the finale stands in as the publication entry.
events.binWhy: The concluding broadcast; not a moment in the story.

events.title: The Observers invade
events.description: Men from the year 2609, who have wrecked their own Earth, come back and take this one. Uprisings are crushed in what survivors call the Purge; collaborators are branded as Loyalists; the Fringe Division is kept on to police the natives; Walter seals himself, Peter and Astrid in amber, and Peter and Olivia's daughter Etta is taken.
events.inUniverse: The invasion begins on the day of a family picnic in a park; the final timeline branches from that same moment

sources.title: Wikipedia: Letters of Transit (on-screen text: in 2015 the Observers took over human society)
Wikipedia: Mythology of Fringe (in 2015 the Observers invaded and instituted the Purge)
Wikipedia: Fringe season 4 ('Letters of Transit': Walter has spent the past 21 years in amber)

events.note: The year is stated in 'Letters of Transit' and season 5. Wikipedia places the final timeline's fixed point in November 2015; the month of the invasion itself is not stated on screen. This is the entry a reader could match against today's news: an occupation of Earth by its own descendants.
events.binWhy: The world is conquered and occupied by a power from its own future.

facets.change: free humanity → natives under occupation

events.title: The Fringe team is freed from amber
events.description: After twenty-one years of occupation, the Observers are changing the atmosphere to suit themselves and Loyalists run the checkpoints. The resistance, with the grown-up Etta inside the Fringe Division, frees Walter, Peter and Astrid from amber, and they start collecting the pieces of a plan to undo the invasion.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Letters of Transit (set in 2036)
Wikipedia: Fringe season 5

events.note: Season 5 is set entirely in 2036, stated on screen. Etta is killed by the Observer commander Windmark partway through the year.
events.binWhy: An occupied people rises against the power from the future that holds them.

facets.change: a crushed occupation → an organised resistance with a plan

events.title: Walter takes Michael to 2167
events.description: Walter carries Michael, an Observer child who has both their intelligence and human feeling, through a wormhole to the Oslo laboratory where the Observers were first engineered. The scientists see that feeling need not be sacrificed; the programme that made the Observers is abandoned, and the invasion of 2015 never happens.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mythology of Fringe (Observers born out of an experiment by a Norwegian scientist in 2167; the finale sends Michael there)
Fringe Wiki: Final Timeline

events.note: The year is stated in 'The Boy Must Live' and the finale. The effect lands in 2015: the reset returns the timeline to the day of the invasion and Walter and Michael are erased from it. This entry is placed at 2167 because that is the date at which the record is changed.
events.binWhy: A traveller arrives from the past and changes the future, cancelling the invasion.

facets.change: a programme that breeds the Observers → a programme abandoned

lineages.groupingNote: A hidden history run by an FBI unit, in the X-Files line: in our universe the public record from 2008 is a set of unexplained disasters, and underneath them are a 1981 drug trial on children, a 1985 breach into a parallel universe and a secret war between the two. It becomes open alternate history only in 2015, when the Observers invade. Fringe has several timelines; this lineage follows the timeline of seasons 4 and 5, in which Peter drowned in 1985 and returned in 2011, because it is the one the series ends in. Events of seasons 1-3 are kept only where both timelines share them (the 1985 crossing, Flight 627, the war between the universes). The 2167 entry is where Walter changes the record, and its effect lands back in 2015. Tiers: T3 holds 1981 and 1985; T2 runs from 2008 to 2167; T4 and T1 are empty, since the Observers' own era (2609) is a future the ending cancels and is not charted.

lineages.title: Harry Potter
lineages.creator: J.K. Rowling

divergence.label: The attack on the Potters
divergence.delta: Real: a quiet suburban family in Surrey raises an orphaned nephew nobody asks about. Fiction: the most feared wizard alive is destroyed by a baby, his followers scatter, and the hidden magical Britain that has been running alongside ours for three centuries gets a hero it cannot protect.
divergence.note: The concealment itself is far older — the International Statute of Secrecy took effect in 1692 — but the branch point that produces the story is Voldemort's attack on 31 October 1981.

ending.why: The dark lord is destroyed, the world he threatened heals, and nineteen years later all is well.

events.title: Hogwarts is founded
events.description: Godric Gryffindor, Salazar Slytherin, Rowena Ravenclaw and Helga Hufflepuff build a castle school in the Scottish highlands, and wizarding Britain acquires the institution that will outlast every Muggle government.
events.note: The books say only that the school was founded over a thousand years before the 1990s; the conventional c. 990 dating is arithmetic from that statement, and the exact year is a convention rather than a stated fact.
events.binWhy: A body is founded that will shape everything after it.

facets.change: a persecuted minority → founds its own school

events.title: The Statute of Secrecy takes effect
events.description: The International Confederation of Wizards puts the Statute of Secrecy fully into force and the magical world withdraws behind concealment charms, memory modification and its own ministries for the next three centuries.
events.note: Instituted in 1689 and implemented in 1692, the same year as the Salem witch trials; the real trials are the Muggle-side event the wizarding law answers.
events.binWhy: The magical world hides itself from everyone else by law.

facets.change: visible → hidden by its own law

events.title: Dumbledore defeats Grindelwald
events.description: Albus Dumbledore defeats the dark wizard Grindelwald and takes the Elder Wand, ending the magical war that ran parallel to the Second World War without either side noticing the other.
events.note: The date is given on Dumbledore's Chocolate Frog card and is deliberately the year the real Second World War ended.
events.binWhy: A battle or campaign settles the war.

facets.change: a hidden war → ended by one duel

events.title: Voldemort is destroyed by a baby
events.description: Voldemort murders Lily and James Potter and is annihilated trying to kill their son, ending the first wizarding war overnight and leaving Harry alive, famous and hidden with his Muggle relatives in Surrey.
events.note: Dated by the books' own chronology: Harry is fifteen months old at the attack and turns eleven in 1991.
events.binWhy: The dark lord is destroyed; his war ends overnight and the survivor is hidden.

facets.change: the dark lord ascendant → destroyed trying to kill a child

events.title: The letters from Hogwarts
events.description: Harry Potter turns eleven, Hagrid arrives with his Hogwarts letter, and he learns that his parents were murdered by a wizard and that he is famous in a world the Dursleys have never heard of.
events.note: The first book opens on Harry's eleventh birthday, 31 July 1991, ten years after the attack that made him the Boy Who Lived.
events.binWhy: An ordinary person is drawn into the larger story.

facets.change: an ordinary boy → told who he is and where he belongs

events.title: The Chamber of Secrets opens
events.description: The Heir of Slytherin reopens the Chamber of Secrets and a basilisk petrifies Muggle-born students, the first sign in the series that the hidden world's own civil war will spill into the ordinary one.
events.note: The second book spans the 1992-1993 school year.
events.binWhy: Students attacked inside the school by a hidden enemy within.

facets.change: a school → attacked from within by a hidden enemy

events.title: Voldemort returns and is disbelieved
events.description: Voldemort is restored to a body in the Little Hangleton graveyard, and the Ministry of Magic spends the following year running a press campaign denying it — the archetype's mechanism in its purest form.
events.note: The third task of the Triwizard Tournament is in June 1995; the denial campaign runs through the 1995-1996 school year.
events.binWhy: The government spends a year denying what it knows.

facets.change: the enemy dead → returned, and officially denied

events.title: The Battle of Hogwarts
events.description: The wizarding war ends in one night inside the castle, with Voldemort killed and the Statute of Secrecy stretched but never broken, so the Muggle world never learns what happened.
events.note: The battle is dated 2 May 1998 by the books' own chronology; it is the last event of the main series' present day.
events.binWhy: A battle or campaign settles the war.

facets.change: the state captured → the war ends in one night

events.title: Nineteen years later
events.description: Harry, Ginny, Hermione and Ron see their own children onto the Hogwarts Express at King's Cross, in a present day that is exactly ours and still completely unaware of them.
events.note: The epilogue sits nineteen years after the battle, which fixes it in 2017 — the year the real-world calendar caught up with the books, and the anchor for this lineage's present day.
events.binWhy: A jump forward shows what the world became.

facets.change: war → a generation later, ordinary life

lineages.groupingNote: Harry Potter's present day is ours: Privet Drive, King's Cross and the Ministry's Muggle Prime Minister are all real, and the branch is a concealment treaty rather than a changed history. The 1692 Statute of Secrecy is the load-bearing event — it shares its year with the Salem witch trials, so the fiction explains a real historical atrocity as the reason the magical world went dark — and the story's own branch opens in 1981, ten years before Harry's first letter. On the real axis most of the lineage sits in the 20th century: two T4 events in the deep past, six T3 events for the 1945-1998 span the books actually narrate, and one T2 event for the 2017 epilogue. The T1 tier is empty because the fiction stops there — at the year the real calendar caught up with it — so no magical future has been invented to reach deep time.

lineages.title: Buffy the Vampire Slayer
lineages.creator: Joss Whedon

divergence.label: The Slayer comes to the Hellmouth
divergence.delta: Real: Sunnydale is an ordinary Southern California town. Fiction: it is built on a Hellmouth, its death rate is the highest in the state, and a teenage girl is the only thing standing between the town and the demons underneath it.
divergence.note: Vampires and demons have existed in secret for all of human history — there is no single break with real history, only the point where the fiction's present day begins; 1997 is where the series and the real calendar coincide.

ending.why: The line of Slayers is shared out and later renewed two centuries on; the fight is never over, which is the point.

events.title: The First Slayer is created
events.description: The Shadow Men chain a young woman to a rock and force the essence of a demon into her, creating the Slayer line — one girl in each generation made strong enough to fight what hides in the dark.
events.inUniverse: the age of the Old Ones
events.note: The origin is shown in flashback but never dated by the show, so year 1 stands for deep prehistory; the lineage's ancient past is this single event rather than a chain of dated ones.
events.binWhy: A girl is made stronger than what hides in the dark.

facets.change: defenceless → one girl made strong enough

events.title: Buffy arrives in Sunnydale
events.description: Buffy Summers moves to Sunnydale, meets her new Watcher and her school library's secret, and within weeks has drowned at the hands of the vampire Master and been revived by Xander — the Hellmouth's activity now the hidden cause of the town's absurd death toll.
events.note: Merges the March arrival with the May season finale, as the schema allows only one event per lineage-year pair; the series' first season is set in its broadcast year, and the show's present stays within a year or two of the real calendar for its whole run.
events.binWhy: An ordinary person is drawn into the larger story.

facets.change: a new town → the chosen girl arrives where the threat is

events.title: The Battle of Sunnydale
events.description: Willow activates every Potential Slayer in the world, the First Evil's army is destroyed and the Hellmouth collapses, leaving one girl's power shared among thousands and a town that no longer exists.
events.note: The televised series ends in May 2003 and the finale's consequences drive the canonical comics that continue the story.
events.binWhy: A battle or campaign settles the war.

facets.change: one chosen → thousands; the enemy destroyed, the town gone

events.title: A vampire becomes a celebrity
events.description: Harmony Kendall rises to fame as a reality television star and ushers in a pro-vampire, anti-Slayer public order — the moment the supernatural stops being a secret and becomes a news cycle.
events.note: The reveal happens in the eighth season of the canonical comics, published 2008-2009; the in-universe date of that season is only pinned by its publication window, so the year is the best-supported reading rather than a stated one.
events.binWhy: The supernatural stops being a secret and becomes a news cycle.

facets.change: a secret world → a celebrity on television

events.title: The Seed is destroyed and magic leaves the world
events.description: Buffy smashes the mystical Seed beneath Sunnydale to stop Twilight, ending the war at the cost of removing magic from the universe: Slayers and vampires keep their power and every witch on Earth loses hers.
events.note: Placed in the publication year of the eighth season's final arc; the comics' chronology is loose and the season is usually read as spanning about a year and a half after 2003.
events.binWhy: Magic leaves the world; every witch loses her power.

facets.change: a world with magic → magic ends to end the war

events.title: Melaka Fray is called
events.description: Two centuries after demons were banished from Earth, the old magic is legend, vampires are dismissed as radiation mutants called lurks, and a teenage thief in a flooded Manhattan becomes the first new Slayer in generations.
events.inUniverse: the 23rd century
events.note: The comic places Melaka two hundred years after Buffy's era and firmly in the 23rd century; year 2200 is a midpoint for that convention, not a stated date. On the real axis the 23rd century is T2 — near future, not deep time — so this is the furthest the fiction reaches without ever leaving our next three hundred years.
events.binWhy: A new Slayer is called after generations.

facets.change: generations without → a new chosen one called

lineages.groupingNote: Buffy hides its whole cosmology under an ordinary American town: the vampires are real, the Hellmouth is real, and the human world's ignorance is the story's standing joke and its tragedy. The branch never changes the historical record, so the lineage has no documented break with real history — the divergence is the point at which the fiction's present begins in 1997, and the 2009 celebrity reveal is where the secrecy finally fails. It is also the only lineage here whose story genuinely leaves the present century: the canonical comics jump two hundred years to the Slayer of the 23rd century, where magic has become legend, vampires have been reclassified as mutants and the Watchers' Council has decayed into fanatics. That is real narrative distance, and the real axis records it faithfully — the 1997-2003 seasons are T3, the 2009-2010 comics and Fray's 2200 are T2, and only the Slayer line's mythological origin sits in T4. Its T1 tier is empty because the fiction stops short of 2300: the story's own deep future is still, on our calendar, only two centuries away.

lineages.title: The War of the Worlds
lineages.creator: H. G. Wells

divergence.label: The Martians land on Horsell Common
divergence.delta: Real: 1907 is an Edwardian summer, and Mars comes to a favourable opposition in July; astronomers still argue over Lowell's canals, and no one sees anything leave the planet. Fiction: ten cylinders fired from Mars fall on the Home Counties, their fighting-machines beat the army and empty London, and within weeks every Martian is dead of Earth's bacteria.
divergence.inUniverse: 'Early in the twentieth century', six years before the narrator writes; June into July. Wells never states the year.
divergence.note: Wells gives weekdays, a June setting and a Mars opposition, but no year. The narrator writes 'six years' after the invasion, and the opening puts it 'early in the twentieth century'. Chronologists who fit the text to the dates of oppositions and weekdays favour 1907 (the princeofcairo chronology settles on 28 June-20 July 1907; a Wellsian article, 'When Was the War of the Worlds?', makes the same case); 1902 and 1905 have also been proposed, and no year fits every clue. The fork is placed at the landing rather than earlier. The 1894 light the narrator reads as the casting of the Martians' gun was a real observation, and he offers that reading as a guess ('I am inclined to think'); he also says unexplained markings were seen near it at the next two oppositions, which is the only fictional observation before the invasion year and is not an event anyone in the novel saw as such.

sources.title: Project Gutenberg: The War of the Worlds by H. G. Wells (full text)
princeofcairo (LiveJournal): War of the Chronology of War of the Worlds (dates the invasion to June-July 1907)
Wikipedia: The War of the Worlds

ending.why: The invaders are dead within weeks, London fills again, and the narrator's epilogue credits the invasion with enormous gifts to science and 'the conception of the commonweal of mankind', while watching Mars for the next attack.

lineages.groupingNote: An alternate past by the passage of time: Wells set the invasion a few years ahead of his 1897 readers, and it is now a twentieth century that did not happen. The lineage follows the 1898 novel only. The adaptations move it: Orson Welles's 1938 broadcast to New Jersey, George Pal's 1953 film to southern California, Spielberg's 2005 film to the present-day American East Coast; none of their dates is used. The novel has only two datable moments of its own, both derived, so the chain says so rather than padding: six of the eight story events are real history the book names or builds on, filed before the fork. Tiers: T4 holds everything before 1900 (the Tasmanian war, Darwin, Schiaparelli, the Lick telescope, the 1894 light, Lowell, and the 1897-98 publications); T3 holds the invasion (1907) and the epilogue (about 1913); T2 and T1 are empty, because Wells looks no further than the next opposition.

sources.title: Wikipedia: The War of the Worlds
Project Gutenberg: The War of the Worlds by H. G. Wells (full text)

events.title: Martial law against Aboriginal Tasmanians
events.description: During the Black War in Van Diemen's Land, Governor George Arthur declares martial law against Aboriginal people; it stays in force for more than three years. A population estimated at 3,000 to 7,000 in 1803 is down to about 220 by 1832-33.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Black War

events.note: Wells's narrator asks readers not to judge the Martians too harshly, because the Tasmanians 'were entirely swept out of existence in a war of extermination waged by European immigrants, in the space of fifty years'. The comparison is the book's moral centre: the Martians do to England what the British Empire did to Tasmania. Wells repeats the belief of his time that no Aboriginal Tasmanians survived; their descendants did.
events.binWhy: A colonial government declares war on a people inside its colony.

facets.change: a frontier war → martial law against a people

events.title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
events.description: Natural selection gives a mechanism for the change of species and a picture of life as a struggle in which the better adapted survive.

sources.title: Wikipedia: On the Origin of Species

events.note: The novel is Darwinian throughout: the Martians are what evolution might make of a mind on an older, cooling world, and they are killed by bacteria against which humans have been armoured, in the narrator's words, 'by the toll of a billion deaths'.
events.binWhy: A theory arrives that the story's ending turns on.

facets.change: fixed species → evolution by natural selection

events.title: Schiaparelli maps the canali of Mars
events.description: At the great opposition of 1877 the Italian astronomer charts long straight markings he calls canali, 'channels'. In English they become 'canals', and with the word comes the idea of Martian engineers.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Giovanni Schiaparelli

events.note: Wells names Schiaparelli in the first chapter as one of the men who watched the red planet and failed to interpret what they mapped.
events.binWhy: An observation arrives that turns Mars into a world that might be inhabited.

facets.change: a red disc → a mapped world with 'canals'

events.title: The Lick refractor sees first light
events.description: The 36-inch refractor on Mount Hamilton, California, becomes the largest refracting telescope in the world, at the first permanently occupied mountain-top observatory.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Lick Observatory

events.note: In the novel the 1894 light on Mars is seen 'first at the Lick Observatory'; in reality Lick observers recorded it on 28 June 1894, a month before Nice.
events.binWhy: A new instrument is switched on that will be first to see the Martians' fire.

facets.change: smaller telescopes → the largest refractor on Earth

events.title: A strange light on Mars
events.description: Observers at the Lick Observatory, then at Nice on 28 July, see a bright projection on the planet; Nature reports it on 2 August 1894 as 'A Strange Light on Mars'.

sources.title: Adam Roberts: The mystery of the Martian lights (Lick 28 June, Nice 28 July, Nature 2 August 1894)

events.note: The observation and the Nature note are real. Wells's narrator is 'inclined to think' it was the casting of the Martians' huge gun; that guess is the novel's first hinge, and it is why the invasion is dated from the opposition that follows.
events.binWhy: An observation arrives that the novel will read as the first sign of the invasion.

facets.change: an unexplained light → the first sign of a Martian gun

events.title: Lowell publishes Mars
events.description: Percival Lowell, who founded his observatory in Arizona in 1894, argues that the canals are irrigation works of an old civilisation making a last effort to survive on a drying planet.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Percival Lowell

events.note: Wikipedia: Lowell's picture of a dying Mars significantly influenced science fiction, starting with Wells, who made the further inference that creatures from a dying planet might invade Earth. The novel's opening, minds on an older, cooling world that look on Earth with envious eyes, is Lowell's Mars with a motive added.
events.binWhy: A theory arrives that turns Mars into a dying civilisation.

facets.change: canals as markings → canals as the works of a dying civilisation

events.title: The War of the Worlds is serialised
events.description: Wells's novel runs in Pearson's Magazine in Britain and Cosmopolitan in the United States.

sources.title: Wikipedia: The War of the Worlds

events.note: Wells moved to Woking in 1895 and, by his own account, went about the district choosing places and people for his Martians to destroy; hence Horsell Common.
events.binWhy: A real-world publication or release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: The War of the Worlds is published as a book
events.description: William Heinemann publishes the novel in London, with Harper & Brothers in the United States.

sources.title: Wikipedia: The War of the Worlds

events.note: The book text is the one this lineage follows.
events.binWhy: A real-world publication or release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: The Martians land in Surrey
events.description: A cylinder falls on Horsell Common near Woking and nine more follow. The Martians burn a deputation with the Heat-Ray, destroy the guns at Weybridge and Shepperton, smother the defences with the Black Smoke and drive London's millions into flight, while the torpedo ram Thunder Child sinks two fighting-machines covering the refugee ships. Within about three weeks every Martian is dead of Earth's bacteria.

sources.title: Project Gutenberg: The War of the Worlds by H. G. Wells (full text)
princeofcairo (LiveJournal): War of the Chronology of War of the Worlds (dates the invasion to June-July 1907)

events.note: Wells's text gives weekdays and a June setting but no year; 1907 is the chronologists' best fit (see the divergence). Ten cylinders are fired from Mars on ten nights. The red weed the Martians bring spreads along the Thames valley and dies of bacteria before they do.
events.binWhy: Humanity meets a non-human intelligence, and it comes to conquer.

facets.change: a planet alone → invaded from Mars

events.title: Signs that the Martians have reached Venus
events.description: Six years on, the astronomer Lessing argues from matching markings on Venus and Mars that the Martians have landed on Venus instead. The narrator ends with a humanity changed: science enriched by what the invaders left, a new sense of the common good of mankind, and dread at every shooting star.

sources.title: Project Gutenberg: The War of the Worlds by H. G. Wells (full text)

events.note: The epilogue is written six years after the invasion and dates the signs on Venus to 'seven months ago'; with the invasion in 1907, that puts them in 1912-13. Lessing's case is presented as a hypothesis, not a fact.
events.binWhy: An outside power founds a settlement on a new world.

facets.change: Mars → a foothold on Venus

lineages.title: Brave New World
lineages.creator: Aldous Huxley

divergence.label: Little Reuben's sleep-lesson
divergence.delta: Real: 1931 - radio is new, sleep-learning is not a science, and Ford is a carmaker in the Depression. Fiction: a boy wakes up reciting a lecture he heard asleep, the principle of hypnopaedia is found, and the long road to a world run by conditioning begins.
divergence.inUniverse: 'twenty-three years after Our Ford's first T-Model'
divergence.note: The novel's world matches ours until 1931: Ford, the Model T, Freud and Shaw are all real. The first thing it describes that did not happen is Little Reuben's case, which the Director dates twenty-three years after the Model T. It is a small event, but it is the one the World State's conditioning descends from, and everything larger (the Nine Years' War of AF 141, World Control) comes long after it. Dates in AF are converted as AF n = 1908 + n, which gives AF 632 = 2540.

Wikipedia: Brave New World (AF 632 = AD 2540; AF counted from the Model T, 1908)

events.title: Ford's Model T goes on sale
events.description: Ford begins producing the Model T, the first car built for mass production on a moving line. The World State will date its calendar from it, and its citizens will make the sign of the T in place of the cross.
events.inUniverse: the year of 'Our Ford's first T-Model', the start of the era After Ford

AF years are converted as AF n = 1908 + n, the convention that makes AF 632 fall in 2540 as Wikipedia gives it; counting 1908 as AF 1 instead would move every date back a year.
events.binWhy: Mass production arrives; the fiction later makes it the founding event of its civilisation.

facets.change: hand-built cars → the assembly-line car

events.title: Little Reuben learns in his sleep
events.description: A Polish boy falls asleep with the radio on and wakes up reciting, word for word, a broadcast lecture by George Bernard Shaw in English, a language he does not know. The doctor who is called writes to the medical press, and the principle of sleep-teaching, hypnopaedia, is discovered, though it will be nearly two centuries before it is put to use.

sources.title: Project Gutenberg Canada: Brave New World (1932 Chatto & Windus text)

events.binWhy: A discovery is made that the World State's conditioning will later be built on.

facets.change: sleep as rest → sleep as a channel for instruction

events.title: Brave New World is published
events.description: Chatto & Windus publish Huxley's novel in London. He wrote it in 1931.

events.title: The Nine Years' War begins
events.description: A world war opens with fourteen thousand aeroplanes, anthrax bombs over Berlin's Kurfürstendamm and the Eighth Arrondissement of Paris, poison gases, and a Russian technique for infecting water supplies. Most of the world's historical monuments are destroyed before it ends, and it brings on the great Economic Collapse.

Wikipedia: Brave New World (AF 632 = AD 2540; AF counted from the Model T, 1908)

The war's name gives its length; nothing else about its course is dated.
events.binWhy: A world war begins, fought with biological and chemical weapons against cities.

facets.change: an uncontrolled world → nine years of gas and anthrax war

events.title: World Control, and the campaign against the Past
events.description: After the war and the Economic Collapse the choice is 'between World Control and destruction', and ten World Controllers take charge. Rule by force fails first: when people refuse compulsory consumption, eight hundred Simple Lifers are machine-gunned at Golders Green and two thousand 'culture fans' gassed in the British Museum. The Controllers turn to slower methods, and to a campaign against the Past that closes the museums, blows up the monuments and suppresses every book published before AF 150.

sources.title: Project Gutenberg Canada: Brave New World (1932 Chatto & Windus text)

AF years are converted as AF n = 1908 + n, the convention that makes AF 632 fall in 2540 as Wikipedia gives it; counting 1908 as AF 1 instead would move every date back a year.
events.binWhy: The warring nations are replaced by one world government; its early massacres and book-burning are part of the same founding.

facets.change: warring nations → ten World Controllers

events.title: Soma goes into production
events.description: In AF 178 the Controllers subsidise two thousand pharmacologists and biochemists to find the perfect drug; six years later soma is in commercial production. It gives a holiday from every bad feeling with none of the drawbacks of alcohol or morphine, and becomes the state's first answer to unhappiness.

events.binWhy: A drug that removes discontent is manufactured and distributed as policy.

facets.change: unrest met with force → a drug for every mood

events.title: Hypnopaedia is used officially
events.description: Sleep-teaching, discovered in Little Reuben's case nearly two centuries before, is adopted by the state, not to teach facts but to teach morals: the same sentences whispered under every child's pillow thousands of times until they become the child's own opinions.

facets.change: taught opinions → opinions installed during sleep

events.title: Cyprus is resettled with Alphas
events.description: The Controllers clear the island of Cyprus of all its inhabitants and resettle it with twenty-two thousand specially prepared Alphas, handing them all its farms and factories to manage for themselves.

facets.change: self-governing Alphas → nineteen thousand dead, rule handed back

events.title: The Savage comes to London
events.description: Bernard Marx and Lenina Crowne visit the Savage Reservation in New Mexico and bring back John, the son of the Director of Hatcheries by a woman lost there years before. John becomes a celebrity, then tries to throw away the Deltas' soma ration at a hospital and starts a riot that is quelled with soma vapour. Mustapha Mond exiles Bernard and Helmholtz Watson to islands; John retreats to an abandoned lighthouse and hangs himself.

lineages.groupingNote: Filed in Alternate Past because its fork is in our past (1931, one year before publication): the book's history is ours up to Ford and Freud and parts from it with Little Reuben, and every AF date after that converts to a real year. It follows Huxley's 1932 novel only, not Brave New World Revisited (1958, an essay) or the 2020 television series. Tiers: T3 for the Model T, the fork and the publication (1908-1932); T2 for the war, World Control, soma and hypnopaedia (2049-2122); T1 for Cyprus and the story itself (2381-2540). T4 is empty because the Director's history begins with Ford.
