lineages.title: Snowpiercer
lineages.creator: Jacques Lob, Benjamin Legrand and Jean-Marc Rochette (comic); Bong Joon-ho and Kelly Masterson (film)

divergence.label: Seventy-nine countries disperse CW-7 to cool the planet
divergence.delta: Real: 2014 - stratospheric aerosol injection is a paper proposal backed by Pinatubo's natural cooling, and the one planned British field test was cancelled in 2012; nothing is sprayed. Fiction: on 1 July 2014, 79 countries fly CW-7 into the upper atmosphere, the Earth freezes, and everyone not on Wilford's train dies.
divergence.inUniverse: CW-7 dispersal begins 1 July 2014 (the film's opening news broadcasts)
divergence.note: The film states the date and the number of countries in its opening broadcasts, and a title card says the world froze soon afterwards. Wilford's train and its globe-circling track must have existed before 2014, but the film never dates them, so the fork sits at the first year the fiction states. Everything before 2014 in this lineage is real history of the geoengineering idea. The fork is a policy decision, not an accident: the world chose to cool itself, which is why the film is often cited in today's debate over solar geoengineering and the private ventures now testing it.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Snowpiercer (2013 film)
Quotes.net: Snowpiercer (79 countries disperse CW-7; Namgoong's crashed airplane 'ten years ago')
Wikipedia: Stratospheric aerosol injection

ending.why: The train and everyone on it but two children are gone and the polar bear shows the outside is alive and thawing, but the film stops with a teenager and a five-year-old who have never lived off the train standing in the snow, and never says whether humanity survives them; Bong calls it hopeful, the story leaves it open.

events.title: Le Transperceneige is serialised in À Suivre
events.description: Jacques Lob and Jean-Marc Rochette's French comic puts the last of humanity on a train that circles a frozen Earth, first class at the front and the poor locked in the tail. Casterman publishes it in the magazine À Suivre.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Le Transperceneige

events.note: The source work. Its freeze comes out of a war rather than a geoengineering programme; the CW-7 dispersal, the 2014 date and the staged revolts are the film's. Later volumes (The Explorers 1999, The Crossing 2000, Terminus 2015) are a different continuity from the film.
events.binWhy: Publication of the source comic; a release, not a moment in the story, so it takes no bin.

events.title: Mount Pinatubo cools the planet
events.description: The climactic eruption of Pinatubo in the Philippines puts a sulphate veil into the stratosphere that cuts sunlight and lowers global temperatures by roughly half a degree for up to three years. It becomes the natural experiment every later proposal to cool the Earth from the sky points to.

sources.title: Wikipedia: 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo
Wikipedia: Stratospheric aerosol injection

events.note: Real history, before the fork. The film does not mention Pinatubo, but CW-7 is a fictional version of the idea Pinatubo proved in principle: aerosols high in the atmosphere can cool the whole planet quickly.
events.binWhy: A measured result - aerosols in the stratosphere cool the globe - that the fiction's divergence is built on.

facets.change: a theory of sulphate cooling → a measured global drop

events.title: Crutzen proposes cooling the Earth with sulphur
events.description: Nobel chemist Paul Crutzen publishes a paper in Climatic Change arguing that deliberately injecting sulphur into the stratosphere should be researched as an emergency brake on warming. It breaks a taboo in climate science and starts the modern field of solar geoengineering.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Stratospheric aerosol injection

events.note: Real history, before the fork. The idea goes back to Mikhail Budyko in 1974; Crutzen's paper is what made it respectable. In our world the only planned British field test (SPICE) was cancelled in 2012 and nothing was dispersed at scale; the film's fork is that in 2014 the world stops arguing and does it.
events.binWhy: A theory of how to engineer the climate arrives from a respected scientist; the fiction's 2014 turns on it.

facets.change: an unspeakable idea → a research programme

events.title: Bong Joon-ho's Snowpiercer is released
events.description: Bong Joon-ho's English-language film of the comic opens in South Korea, with Chris Evans as Curtis and Tilda Swinton, Song Kang-ho and Ed Harris. It moves the freeze to a failed geoengineering programme dated the following year.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Snowpiercer (2013 film)

events.note: South Korean release 1 August 2013; France 30 October 2013; limited US release 27 June 2014. The film was released one year before its own fork date, so for its first audience the CW-7 dispersal was next summer.
events.binWhy: Release of the film this lineage follows; not a story moment, so it takes no bin.

events.title: Seventy-nine countries disperse CW-7
events.description: To stop accelerating global warming, 79 countries begin spraying an artificial cooling compound, CW-7, into the upper atmosphere from aircraft on 1 July 2014. It works far too well: soon afterwards the world freezes and everything outside dies. The only survivors are the people aboard Wilford's train, a perpetual-motion luxury express on a track that circles the globe, the paying passengers in front and those who forced their way on packed into the tail.
events.inUniverse: CW-7 dispersal begins 1 July 2014, 06:00 (opening broadcasts)

sources.title: Wikipedia: Snowpiercer (2013 film)
Quotes.net: Snowpiercer (79 countries disperse CW-7; Namgoong's crashed airplane 'ten years ago')

events.note: The film's opening news broadcasts give the date and the 79 countries, and a title card says the world froze soon after dispersal. The freeze, the extinction outside and the boarding are merged into this one year because the film puts them all in 2014; the tail's later count of seventeen years aboard confirms the boarding year. Wilford's globe-circling line must predate 2014, but the film gives it no year.
events.binWhy: A planetary technology - stratospheric cooling - is switched on and changes what the world can do, catastrophically. It is the divergence.

facets.change: a warming planet → a frozen one with one train left

events.title: The tail eats its weak
events.description: The people in the tail boarded with nothing, and within a month of boarding they were eating the weak. Curtis, then a teenager, was about to kill a baby when the tail's elder Gilliam cut off his own arm and offered it instead; others followed, and the killing stopped. The front then began feeding the tail protein blocks, which remain its only food for the next seventeen years.
events.inUniverse: The first month after boarding

sources.title: Wikiquote: Snowpiercer (film dialogue: CW-7, 'After a month, we ate the weak', '18 years I've hated Wilford', the list of revolts)

events.note: Curtis tells this in his confession near the engine ('After a month, we ate the weak'). The film gives no calendar date beyond 'a month' after boarding; 2015 is chosen as the first full year aboard because 2014 is occupied by the dispersal, and the event could equally fall at the end of 2014. The baby Curtis nearly killed is Edgar, who dies in the 2031 revolution.
events.binWhy: Starvation and cannibalism kill the weakest of the tail and shape the tail's society for good.

facets.change: stowaways without food → a tail fed from the front

events.title: The Revolt of the Seven
events.description: Seven passengers rise against the train and get off it, betting they can live on the ice. They freeze a few yards from the track, and their bodies become a landmark the train passes every year, used in the schoolroom as the lesson on why no one leaves.
events.inUniverse: The train's third year

sources.title: This is Barry: Snowpiercer plot and ending explained (Revolt of the Seven three years after departure)
Wikiquote: Snowpiercer (film dialogue: CW-7, 'After a month, we ate the weak', '18 years I've hated Wilford', the list of revolts)

events.note: Wilford names the Revolt of the Seven as the first of the revolts he allowed; the frozen seven are seen through the window. The year rests on the reading, given in plot guides but not on screen as a date, that it happened in the train's third year; with boarding in 2014 that is 2016. Fan readings that the leader was Yona's mother are not stated clearly enough in the film to use.
events.binWhy: A group on the train revolts against the order that holds it; the revolt is lost and becomes a taboo.

facets.change: seven rebels → seven frozen bodies by the track

events.title: The ice starts giving back a crashed airliner
events.description: Every New Year the train passes a crashed airliner buried beside the track. The security specialist Namgoong Minsoo, who designed the train's doors, notices that ten years before the film only its tail showed; by 2031 its body and wings are out of the snow. He concludes the ice is melting and that people could live outside, and keeps it to himself.

sources.title: Quotes.net: Snowpiercer (79 countries disperse CW-7; Namgoong's crashed airplane 'ten years ago')

events.note: Derived from Namgoong's line 'All I saw ten years ago was just the tail' in the 2031 film, which dates the first sign he saw to about 2021. The film does not say when the thaw began, only that it is under way; the year marks Namgoong's first evidence, not the start of the thaw.
events.binWhy: An observation that the world outside is recovering - the fact the ending turns on - is made by one man and not shared.

facets.change: a dead frozen world → a world visibly thawing

events.title: The MacGregor Riots
events.description: The tail rises again and is shot down. Afterwards the tail believes the front spent its last bullets on the riot; the guards who come back to count them carry rifles Curtis is sure are empty.
events.inUniverse: Four years before the film

sources.title: Wikiquote: Snowpiercer (film dialogue: CW-7, 'After a month, we ate the weak', '18 years I've hated Wilford', the list of revolts)

events.note: Curtis dates the last revolt to four years before the film: 'They used up all their bullets four years ago in the last revolt. Bullets are extinct.' Wilford later names the MacGregor Riots among the revolts he allowed. The bullets were not in fact gone; the front was holding them back.
events.binWhy: The tail rises against the front again and is put down by gunfire.

facets.change: a tail revolt → a massacre and apparently empty guns

events.title: Curtis's revolution and the Yekaterina tunnel
events.description: When the front takes two tail children, Curtis bets the guards' guns are empty and leads the tail forward, frees Namgoong from the prison car in exchange for Kronole, and finds the protein blocks are ground insects. In the dark tunnel before the Yekaterina Bridge the front's axe-men meet them; both sides stop to count down the New Year as the train crosses the bridge, then the slaughter resumes. Curtis gets through, but the guards turn out to have bullets after all, and Edgar is among the many killed on the way forward.
events.inUniverse: AD 2031, seventeen years after CW-7

sources.title: Wikipedia: Snowpiercer (2013 film)
Wikiquote: Snowpiercer (film dialogue: CW-7, 'After a month, we ate the weak', '18 years I've hated Wilford', the list of revolts)

events.note: The film is set in 2031, seventeen years after the dispersal. The Yekaterina Bridge crossing marks each year of the train's circuit and is celebrated as New Year; Wilford later says the revolt was meant to end at the Yekaterina tunnel.
events.binWhy: The subjugated tail revolts against the front that feeds and culls it.

facets.change: a caged tail → a revolt moving car by car

events.title: The engine, the bomb and the avalanche
events.description: In the engine Wilford tells Curtis that every revolt was arranged with Gilliam to cull the tail and keep the train in balance, and offers him the engine; Curtis turns it down when he sees a tail child working inside the machine as a replacement part. Namgoong and Yona blow the door with Kronole, the blast brings down an avalanche and the train derails, killing everyone aboard except Yona and the child Timmy. The two climb out into the snow and see a polar bear.
events.inUniverse: The train's eighteenth year, after the New Year crossing

sources.title: Wikipedia: Snowpiercer (2013 film)
Looper: The ending of Snowpiercer explained (Bong Joon-ho on the polar bear and the survivors)

events.note: The film spans the train's New Year: the countdown at the Yekaterina Bridge falls mid-revolution, before the engine scenes. The film opens in 2031, and at the engine Curtis says '18 years I've hated Wilford' where earlier he counted seventeen in the tail, so the climax is filed in the new year, 2032. Some readers count the eighteen years to 2031; the whole film takes place over a few days either side of the crossing. Bong has said everyone on the train dies but the two children.
events.binWhy: The train - the whole of human society - is destroyed and does not come back; its ruler dies with it.

facets.change: a sealed class train → wreckage and two children in the snow

lineages.groupingNote: Belongs in post-industrial collapse because an industrial civilisation ends itself - here by a deliberate technical fix for its own emissions - and what is left is one closed machine run as a class hierarchy. It follows Bong Joon-ho's 2013 film only; the comic (a different cause of the freeze and a different history) and the TNT/AMC series (2020-2024, set seven years after the freeze, with Wilford arriving later on a second train) are separate continuities and appear only in the notes and reading list. Tiers: T3 holds the comic and Pinatubo; T2 holds everything from 2006 to the derailment. There is no T4 because the fiction reaches back only to real climate science, and no T1 because the film ends within a few days of the train's New Year in 2031-2032.

lineages.title: Parable of the Sower
lineages.creator: Octavia E. Butler

divergence.label: The Pox begins, as journalists date it
divergence.delta: Real: 2015. Climate, inequality and a hollowed-out state are in the news, but the institutions still hold. Fiction: this is when the slide the books call the Pox is usually said to start. Nobody fixes the climate, the economy or the social problems, and by the 2020s American towns are walled, water costs more than food, and fire and debt stand in for government.
divergence.inUniverse: Parable of the Talents opens with Bankole's memoir: journalists date 'the Apocalypse', or more often 'the Pox', from 2015 through 2030. Bankole says it began well before 2015 and has not ended.
divergence.note: The books give 2015 as the start of the Pox, and it is the only start year they state. Bankole, who is 57 in 2032 and lived through the whole thing, says the slide began well before 2015, possibly before 2000, and was the result of refusing to deal with obvious climatic, economic and social problems rather than a run of bad luck. So there is no single fork. There is an unchecked drift, and 2015 is the conventional date the world of the novels puts on it. The first dated journal entry, Lauren's fifteenth birthday on 20 July 2024, is already deep inside the decline, so it cannot be the divergence. 2015 is used because it is the novels' own date for the period, and it is marked medium because the novels also argue with that date.

sources.title: ReadingGroupGuides: Parable of the Talents excerpt (Bankole's account of the Pox, 2015-2030)
Wikipedia: Parable of the Talents (novel)

ending.why: By 2090 Jarret is disgraced, Earthseed is a world movement that pays for scholarships, and its first shuttles have lifted colonists to the starship Christopher Columbus. The cost is also on the page: Acorn was destroyed, Lauren's daughter never forgives her, and Lauren dies soon after the launch at 81.

events.title: Parable of the Sower is published
events.description: Octavia E. Butler publishes the first Earthseed novel. It is Lauren Olamina's journal from 2024 to 2027, written from the early 1990s about a California thirty years ahead.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Parable of the Sower (novel)

events.note: Published by Four Walls Eight Windows in 1993. The book extrapolates from the California of the early 1990s: the Los Angeles riots, drought, privatisation and the growth of gated communities.
events.binWhy: A publication, not an event in the story; it has no bin.

events.title: Parable of the Talents is published
events.description: The second novel follows the story from 2032 to 2090 through Lauren's journals, her husband's memoir and her daughter's commentary. Butler's planned third book, Parable of the Trickster, was never finished, so this one ends the chain.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Parable of the Talents (novel)

events.note: Published by Seven Stories Press in 1998. It won the Nebula Award for Best Novel.
events.binWhy: A publication, not an event in the story; it has no bin.

events.title: The Pox: the slow collapse begins
events.description: Climate change, economic collapse and social breakdown compound, and nothing is done about any of them. Over the next fifteen years the public order of the United States falls apart: water and food prices soar, cities burn, and anyone who can afford it lives behind walls.
events.inUniverse: Journalists date 'the Apocalypse' or 'the Pox' from 2015 through 2030 (Parable of the Talents, Bankole's memoir)

sources.title: ReadingGroupGuides: Parable of the Talents excerpt

events.note: The years 2015-2030 are the journalists' dating as the novel reports it. Bankole rejects both ends of it: the Pox began earlier, and it has not ended. What the fiction adds to our 2015 is not a single shock but the failure of every correction.
events.binWhy: Public order breaks down across the country and, as the books tell it, does not come back in its old form.

facets.change: a strained republic → walled enclaves and open road

events.title: Christopher Donner is elected president
events.description: Donner wins the presidency promising to dismantle the space programme and suspend 'overly restrictive' minimum-wage, environmental and worker-protection laws for employers who take on homeless workers in exchange for room and board. That opens the door to company towns and debt bondage.
events.inUniverse: Lauren's journal entry of 6 November 2024 records Donner's win

sources.title: Shmoop: Parable of the Sower chapter 3 summary (entries July-November 2024)
LitCharts: President Christopher Donner

events.note: The journal entry is dated 6 November 2024. In the real calendar that is the day after the 2024 US presidential election, which is one reason the novel has been so widely reread. The election itself is lawful. Its effect in the story is to hand labour and land to whoever can pay for them.
events.binWhy: The nearest bin: the state passes, by election rather than force, to a man who uses it to strip labour and environmental law.

facets.change: labour protections → labour for room and board

events.title: Lauren Olamina names Earthseed
events.description: A fifteen-year-old preacher's daughter in the walled Los Angeles-area neighbourhood of Robledo gives a name, Earthseed, to the verses she has been writing. Their core claim is that God is Change. By her sixteenth birthday she has added the belief that everything later turns on: the destiny of Earthseed is to take root among the stars.
events.inUniverse: Journal entry of Saturday 26 April 2025; the destiny verse follows on 20 July 2025, her sixteenth birthday

sources.title: Shmoop: Parable of the Sower chapter 7 summary (entries April-July 2025)

events.note: Lauren commits to writing the verses in August 2024 and names them in April 2025. She was born on 20 July 2009 and has hyperempathy syndrome, which makes her feel the pain she sees. Nothing in our 2025 corresponds to this; the event is private and matters only for what it later becomes.
events.binWhy: An ordinary teenager starts the belief system the rest of the chain turns on.

facets.change: private verses → a named faith

events.title: Olivar sells itself to KSF
events.description: The coastal city of Olivar votes to privatise itself and hands its land, jobs and policing to the multinational Kagimoto, Stamm, Frampton and Company. Residents get safety in exchange for low wages and rent paid to their employer. It is the company town Donner's labour rules made possible, and Lauren sees it as slavery by debt.
events.inUniverse: Discussed in Lauren's journal entries of 17-31 October 2026

sources.title: Shmoop: Parable of the Sower chapter 11 summary (entries October 2026)
Shmoop: Lauren Olamina timeline

events.note: The year is the year of the journal entries in which Lauren hears of the takeover and KSF advertises for teachers. The novel treats it as recent news, so the vote may have come slightly earlier. Keith's death (August 2026) and her father's disappearance (later that year) fall in the same stretch and are left out to keep one event per year.
events.binWhy: A corporation takes over the running of a city and becomes its landlord, employer and police. That is a new kind of governing body, not just a change of ruler.

facets.change: a city → a company town

events.title: Robledo is overrun and burned; the survivors walk north
events.description: Raiders, many of them addicts of the fire drug 'pyro', drive a truck through Robledo's gate, loot it, burn the houses and shoot the residents. Lauren's family is among the dead. She walks north up the ruined highways with a few survivors, preaching Earthseed as the group grows, and on 10 October 2027 they settle on Bankole's land in the hills near Cape Mendocino and name the place Acorn.
events.inUniverse: Journal entry of 31 July 2027 records the raid; Acorn is named in the entry of 10 October 2027

sources.title: Wikipedia: Parable of the Sower (novel) (2027 attack; Acorn founded near Cape Mendocino)
Fordham Eloquentia Perfecta: Change, Liberation, and Freedom in Parable of the Sower (Robledo destroyed 31 July 2027)
Shmoop: Lauren Olamina timeline (Acorn founded 10 October 2027)

events.note: The raid and the founding of Acorn happen in the same year, so they are merged into one event. The bin describes the raid because that is what the event is; the walk north and Acorn are its result, and Acorn is what the 2033 event destroys. In our July 2027 there is nothing to compare, but readers match this moment against walled suburbs, wildfire and drug epidemics.
events.binWhy: A targeted massacre of a single walled community, short of war, that sends its survivors into exile and leads to a new settlement.

facets.change: a walled street → ashes and a road north

events.title: Andrew Steele Jarret wins the presidency
events.description: A senator from Texas and leader of the Church of Christian America wins the White House on the slogan 'Make America Great Again'. His followers want a Christian nation. They burn 'witches', attack people of other faiths, and treat order as something to restore by force. The zealots he refuses to restrain become his Crusaders.
events.inUniverse: The 2032 election, followed in Lauren's journal and Bankole's memoir from September 2032

sources.title: Wikipedia: Parable of the Talents (novel) (Jarret, 'Make America Great Again')
EBSCO Research Starters: Parable of the Sower and Parable of the Talents

events.note: The novel dates the election to 2032. The month is marked medium because it is inferred from the US electoral calendar, not read off a journal entry. The slogan was already an American campaign phrase before 1998, but it is why the book was widely reread after 2016.
events.binWhy: A religious movement's leader takes control of the federal state by election on a platform of forced conversion, which is a seizure in everything but the method.

facets.change: a secular republic in ruins → a Christian America

events.title: Crusaders overrun Acorn and make it Camp Christian
events.description: Jarret's Crusaders come to Acorn in armoured vehicles, take it, and turn it into a re-education camp. The adults are held in electronic shock collars and made to work, and they are raped and tortured. The children, including Lauren's infant daughter Larkin, are taken and placed with Christian America families.
events.inUniverse: September 2033, when Larkin is about two months old

sources.title: Books That Slay: Parable of the Talents summary (September 2033 attack)
Wikipedia: Parable of the Talents (novel)

events.note: Dated September 2033 in the novel's journal sequence. Larkin is renamed Asha Vere and raised in Seattle, and Lauren does not find her for more than thirty years. The camp is run by zealots whom the government never officially owns, and that distance is what lets it happen.
events.binWhy: A movement in power attacks a religious minority's community, enslaves the adults and takes the children.

facets.change: a free commune → a slave camp

events.title: The prisoners of Camp Christian rise and scatter
events.description: After about seventeen months, a landslide knocks out the control system for the collars. The prisoners kill their guards, take what they can and burn the camp. Lauren decides Earthseed can no longer live as one visible commune and sends its people out to live and teach separately.
events.inUniverse: Early 2035, seventeen months after the September 2033 capture

sources.title: Books That Slay: Parable of the Talents summary (2035 overthrow)
Wikipedia: Parable of the Talents (novel) (2035 rebellion)

events.note: Wikipedia and several guides give 2035. The month follows from the seventeen-month captivity counted from September 2033.
events.binWhy: An enslaved group revolts and kills the people holding it.

facets.change: collared prisoners → a scattered faith

events.title: Jarret is voted out after one term
events.description: The public turns on Jarret over the war he waged against Alaska and Canada and over revelations about Crusader witch-burnings. He loses after a single term, Christian America loses its hold on the state, and the country moves slowly toward a post-war recovery in which Earthseed can grow.
events.inUniverse: Jarret is defeated in the 2036 election

sources.title: Wikipedia: Parable of the Talents (novel) (Jarret defeated after a single term)

events.note: 2036 follows from a single term that began in January 2033. The novel does not stage the vote; it reports the result and its causes. Christian America survives as a church and as the family that raises Asha, but it is out of power.
events.binWhy: A ruler leaves office in disgrace and his movement loses the state.

facets.change: a crusading president → a disgraced one

events.title: Earthseed is famous, and Asha finds her mother
events.description: The movement that started with verses in Portland and wealthy converts is now national and international. It funds scholarships, runs its own communities and keeps pressing for the stars. Asha Vere, now 34, sees her own face in its founder, learns she is Larkin, and meets Lauren, but she will not forgive her for choosing Earthseed over the search.
events.inUniverse: Asha is 34 when she meets Lauren

sources.title: Books That Slay: Parable of the Talents summary (2067 reunion)
Spoil The Ending: The ending of Parable of the Talents (Asha is 34)

events.note: Derived: Larkin is born in 2033 and is 34 at the meeting, which gives 2067, or early 2068 depending on her birthday. The novel covers Earthseed's growth from the late 2030s to the 2060s in summary rather than dated events, so this meeting is the dated point that shows how far it has come.
events.binWhy: The story jumps three decades to show what Earthseed and the country have become.

facets.change: a hunted sect → a rich, famous movement

events.title: The first Earthseed shuttles leave for the Christopher Columbus
events.description: Shuttles lift Earthseed colonists to the starship Christopher Columbus. They travel in suspended animation with embryos and seeds, bound for humanity's first colony on a world around another star. Lauren, 81, watches the launch and dies soon after, estranged from her daughter.
events.inUniverse: Lauren's final journal entry, 2090

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters: Parable of the Sower and Parable of the Talents (2090 launch)
Wikipedia: Parable of the Talents (novel) (Christopher Columbus; Lauren dies at 81)

events.note: 2090 is stated, and it squares with Lauren's birth in July 2009 and her age of 81. Butler meant Parable of the Trickster to follow the colonists to the planet Bow, but she abandoned it, so the launch is where the published chain ends. Earthseed chose the ship's name, and the novel leaves the irony of naming it after Columbus in plain view.
events.binWhy: The first colony ship leaves for a star no one has reached.

facets.change: a destiny in verse → colonists in orbit

lineages.groupingNote: It belongs in post-industrial-collapse because nothing cuts this world off from ours. Industrial America runs itself down through climate, debt and neglect (the Pox), and the story is about what gets built in the wreckage, from a walled street to a theocracy to a religion aimed at the stars. Continuity is the two published novels only; the abandoned Parable of the Trickster is not used. T3 holds only the two publications (1993, 1998), and every story event from the 2015 fork to the 2090 launch is T2. T4 is empty because the novels give no history before the late twentieth century. T1 is empty because the published chain ends in 2090 as the ship leaves.

lineages.title: Station Eleven
lineages.creator: Emily St. John Mandel (novel); Patrick Somerville (HBO Max series)

divergence.label: The Georgia Flu reaches Toronto
divergence.delta: Real: 2015 — the West African Ebola epidemic is being brought under control and no influenza pandemic comes. Fiction: a flu from the Republic of Georgia kills almost everyone on Earth within weeks, and the grid, the internet and every government go with them.
divergence.inUniverse: Year Zero: the winter night Arthur Leander dies playing King Lear in Toronto. The novel never names a calendar year.
divergence.note: Station Eleven counts time from the collapse (Year One, Year Fifteen, Year Twenty) and never states the calendar year of the outbreak; readers asking the question are told only that it starts in the present. The book was written in the early 2010s and published in September 2014, and its pre-collapse chapters are the world of its first readers, down to the iPhones and laptops in Clark's museum. The atlas therefore places Year Zero in the first Toronto winter after publication, 2015 (the opening night is snowy), which keeps the outbreak in its readers' present without predating the book. A reader who takes 2013 or 2014 moves every date here back by one or two years; nothing in the text rules either out. The 2021 HBO series sets its outbreak in its own present, December 2020; that is its continuity, not the novel's. The novel's pre-collapse flashbacks (Arthur's marriages, Miranda's comic) are counted in years before the outbreak and are not dated here.

events.title: Emily St. John Mandel publishes Station Eleven
events.description: Knopf and HarperCollins Canada publish the novel in September 2014. It opens on a winter night in Toronto in a world indistinguishable from its readers' own, then moves between that world's last years and the twentieth year after it ends.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Station Eleven (novel)

events.note: First published 9 September 2014; it won the Arthur C. Clarke Award in 2015 and was a National Book Award finalist. The publication precedes the atlas's Year Zero by a few months, which is deliberate: see divergence.note.
events.binWhy: A publication date is not a moment in the story.

events.title: Arthur Leander dies on stage, and the Georgia Flu reaches Toronto
events.description: A fifty-one-year-old film star has a heart attack playing King Lear in Toronto; that same night a doctor at Toronto General warns his friend that a flu first reported in the Republic of Georgia is filling the hospital. It spreads faster than anything he has seen, and within weeks it has killed something like ninety-nine per cent of the world.
events.inUniverse: Year Zero: the night of Arthur Leander's King Lear, in winter (snow in Toronto)

sources.title: Wikipedia: Station Eleven (novel)
GradeSaver: Station Eleven section 1 (Arthur, fifty-one, dies playing Lear)
LitCharts: Station Eleven chapter 1 (the King Lear night; snow in Toronto)

events.note: The novel gives no calendar year for the outbreak; it counts time from it. The atlas takes 2015, the first Toronto winter after the book's publication, as Year Zero; the reasoning and the alternatives are in divergence.note. Everything else here, the theatre night, the flu's origin in Georgia and its speed, is stated in the text.
events.binWhy: A new influenza kills almost everyone alive in a few weeks; that is the plague bin by definition.

facets.change: an ordinary winter → ninety-nine per cent of humanity dead within weeks

events.title: The lights do not come back
events.description: Within the first month the internet, the electrical grid and running water fail, and in the year that follows nothing restarts: no government, no rescue, no news. At Severn City, a small Great Lakes airport where flights were diverted on the first day, the stranded passengers become a settlement, and on Day 100 Clark Thompson puts his dead iPhone and laptop in a display case and starts the Museum of Civilization.
events.inUniverse: Year One (the grid and the internet fail in the first weeks of the flu; the museum begins on Day 100)

sources.title: The Bibliofile: Station Eleven recap, with the novel's Day and Year markers
Wikipedia: Station Eleven (novel)
LitCharts: Station Eleven plot summary

events.note: The novel's recaps place the failures of internet, power and water in the first thirty days and the museum on Day 100, which may fall in the same calendar year as the outbreak; the event is dated to Year One, the novel's name for the first year after, and merges the collapse with the airport's founding because they fall in the same span. The Year label is the novel's; the calendar year is Year Zero = 2015 plus that count (see divergence.note), so the whole chain moves with that choice.
events.binWhy: The order of the industrial world breaks and does not return: the grid, the internet and the state are gone for good. The airport town is what survives inside that collapse.

facets.change: a grounded flight and a failing grid → no power, no internet, no state, and a town inside an airport

events.title: Tyler and Elizabeth leave the airport with a religious group
events.description: Arthur's son Tyler, a child at the airport who reads the New Testament alongside the Station Eleven comics his father gave him, has come to believe the dead were not good enough to be spared. He and his mother Elizabeth leave Severn City with a wandering group of believers; he will grow up to lead it.
events.inUniverse: Year Two

sources.title: The Bibliofile: Station Eleven recap, with the novel's Day and Year markers
LitCharts: Tyler Leander / the Prophet

events.note: Year Two for the departure is stated in the novel's airport chapters. The Year label is the novel's; the calendar year is Year Zero = 2015 plus that count (see divergence.note), so the whole chain moves with that choice.
events.binWhy: A boy leaves convinced that the survivors were chosen and the dead were judged; the cult he will lead turns on that belief.

facets.change: a stranded boy → a believer that the flu was a judgment, gone with a cult

events.title: Jeevan Chaudhary walks into McKinley and becomes its doctor
events.description: Jeevan, the would-be paramedic who tried to save Arthur, walks south for years and reaches McKinley, a farming settlement of a few dozen families in what was Virginia. He becomes its doctor, marries one of its founders in Year Ten and raises a family there.
events.inUniverse: Year Three

sources.title: The Bibliofile: Station Eleven recap, with the novel's Day and Year markers

events.note: Year Three for his arrival and Year Ten for his marriage to Daria are stated in the novel; the settlement's own founding predates his arrival by an unstated span, so the event is dated to his arrival. The Year label is the novel's; the calendar year is Year Zero = 2015 plus that count (see divergence.note), so the whole chain moves with that choice.
events.binWhy: A permanent farming settlement takes root in new, empty country; it is the first place in the chain where the collapse turns into ordinary life.

facets.change: a man walking south → the doctor of a permanent settlement in what was Virginia

events.title: The Travelling Symphony takes to the road
events.description: A group of musicians sets out between the settlements of the Great Lakes, merges a few months later with a company of actors, and becomes the Travelling Symphony: horse-drawn caravans, an orchestra and Shakespeare on a two-year circuit. The lead caravan carries a line from Star Trek: Voyager, 'Survival is insufficient'.
events.inUniverse: Year Five

events.note: The novel states the Symphony has travelled since Year Five. Kirsten, eight at the outbreak, joins it after her brother's death; its actors perform only Shakespeare because audiences want the best of the old world. The Year label is the novel's; the calendar year is Year Zero = 2015 plus that count (see divergence.note), so the whole chain moves with that choice.
events.binWhy: A lasting body is founded that carries a culture between isolated towns; it is the story's central institution.

facets.change: scattered survivors with instruments → a touring company carrying Shakespeare between towns

events.title: HBO Max releases the Station Eleven miniseries
events.description: Patrick Somerville's ten-episode adaptation premieres on HBO Max, moving the outbreak to Chicago and to its own present, and giving Tyler a redemption the novel does not.

events.title: The New Petoskey News interviews Kirsten Raymonde
events.description: François Diallo, who keeps a library and prints a newspaper in New Petoskey, interviews Kirsten about the old world and the first years after. She remembers almost nothing of Year One on the road with her brother, and carries tattooed knives for the people she has killed.

facets.change: fifteen unrecorded years → a newspaper asking survivors what they remember

events.title: The Prophet holds St. Deborah by the Water
events.description: The cult Tyler grew up in, now armed and led by him as the Prophet, controls the lakeside town of St. Deborah by the Water and takes young girls as his wives. Two Symphony members who had stayed there with their newborn flee to Severn City, and from their description Clark realises the Prophet is Tyler.

LitCharts: Tyler Leander / the Prophet

The Symphony left Charlie and Jeremy at St. Deborah on its previous pass two years before Year Twenty, and they reach the airport in Year Nineteen, so the Prophet held the town by then; dated to Year Nineteen. The Year label is the novel's; the calendar year is Year Zero = 2015 plus that count (see divergence.note), so the whole chain moves with that choice.
events.binWhy: An armed religious faction takes control of a town and rules it by doctrine and force.

events.title: The Prophet is killed, and electric light is seen to the south
events.description: The Symphony passes through St. Deborah, is hunted by the Prophet's men and loses members; when he holds Kirsten at gunpoint on the road she answers him with lines from Station Eleven, and the boy guarding him shoots him and then himself. At Severn City the Symphony finds its missing members, and Clark takes Kirsten up the control tower to see, through a telescope, a town to the south lit by electric streetlamps.
events.inUniverse: Year Twenty (July onward)

The bin follows the confrontation, the event's action; the lights, which another town switched on offstage, carry the ending. The Year label is the novel's; the calendar year is Year Zero = 2015 plus that count (see divergence.note), so the whole chain moves with that choice.

lineages.groupingNote: Belongs in Post-Industrial Collapse because its fork is a single catastrophe in our own present, a pandemic that ends the grid and the state within weeks, and the story is about what the survivors keep. The novel follows one continuity (Mandel's 2014 text); the 2021 series moves the outbreak to 2020 and Chicago and softens the Prophet, and is recorded only as a release. Every event is T2 (2014-2035). T3 and T4 are empty because the pre-collapse chapters reach back only a few decades into Arthur's life and are counted in years before the outbreak rather than dated; T1 is empty because the story ends in Year Twenty.

lineages.title: Seveneves
lineages.creator: Neal Stephenson

divergence.label: The Moon breaks apart (A+0.0.0)
divergence.delta: Real: the Moon is where it has been for four billion years, and the ISS is a ten-person laboratory due for retirement. Fiction: at 05:03:12 UTC an unknown agent shatters the Moon into seven pieces, and within days the ISS is being rebuilt as the hub of an ark, because the world has two years left.
divergence.inUniverse: A+0.0.0, 'Zero'; the novel counts all time from the breakup and never gives a calendar year
divergence.note: Seveneves states no calendar year. Its first two parts are set in its readers' present: today's ISS (called Izzy), today's rockets and spaceplanes, a science broadcaster modelled on the ones we have. Following the convention the atlas uses for Station Eleven, Zero is placed in the first year after publication (May 2015), 2016, so that the fork sits in its first readers' present without predating the book. Every later year is that anchor plus the novel's own offsets (701 days to the Hard Rain, three years to the Cleft, five thousand years to Part Three), so all of them inherit this uncertainty.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Seveneves
Berkeley Science Review: Neal Stephenson's Seveneves, a low-spoiler science review

ending.why: Five thousand years on, three billion descendants of seven women live in a ring around a re-greening Earth, and the discovery that other humans survived on the planet reunites the species, even as Red and Blue keep up a cold war.

events.title: The ISS is permanently crewed
events.description: Expedition 1 boards the International Space Station and people have lived in orbit continuously ever since. In the novel this station, enlarged and bolted to an iron asteroid, becomes the hub of the Cloud Ark and then the ship Endurance.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Expedition 1 (docked 2 November 2000)
Wikipedia: International Space Station

events.note: Real history the whole novel rests on. Stephenson's Izzy is 'a mildly beefed up fictional version' of the ISS, in the Berkeley Science Review's phrase, so the real station's permanent occupation is the root of the book's ark.
events.binWhy: A permanently inhabited outpost is established off the planet.

facets.change: visits to orbit → people living there permanently

events.title: The X-37 spaceplane flies in orbit
events.description: The US Air Force launches Boeing's uncrewed X-37B on its first orbital mission. In the novel a crewed X-37 is the vehicle the President uses to break the ark's rules and get herself into orbit as the Hard Rain begins.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Boeing X-37 (first spaceflight 22 April 2010)
Wikipedia: Seveneves (Flaherty flees to the ISS aboard an X-37)

events.note: Real history. The real X-37B is uncrewed and its missions are secret; the novel's version carries the President, her science adviser and his gun.
events.binWhy: A reusable military spaceplane is put into service; the fiction turns it into an escape vehicle.

facets.change: expendable capsules → a reusable spaceplane

events.title: Seveneves is published
events.description: William Morrow publishes the 880-page novel: two parts in the present day, one five thousand years later.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Seveneves (published 19 May 2015)

events.binWhy: A real-world publication date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: The Moon breaks, and Earth is given two years
events.description: An unexplained agent splits the Moon into seven large fragments. The astronomer and broadcaster Doc Dubois works out that the pieces will grind each other down exponentially and rain onto Earth as a 'Hard Rain' that will boil the oceans and sterilise the surface for thousands of years; governments start building a Cloud Ark of small habitats around the ISS and choose who goes by a global Casting of Lots.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Seveneves (Part One)

events.note: The time of day is in the novel; the year is the atlas's convention (see the divergence note). The agent is never explained, which is the book's point: the plot is what people do with a deadline, not the cause. In our 2016 the Moon is intact and asteroid deflection is still a study programme; NASA's DART probe would not strike an asteroid until 2022.
events.binWhy: The breakup matters because of the calculation that follows: a result that gives every later decision its deadline.

facets.change: an intact Moon → a two-year countdown

events.title: The Hard Rain
events.description: Moon fragments begin entering the atmosphere 701 days after Zero, and the sky turns white with fire. About 1,500 people are in orbit; nearly every living thing on the surface dies.
events.inUniverse: A+701 days

sources.title: Wikipedia: Seveneves (the Hard Rain begins 701 days after the destruction of the Moon)

events.note: 701 days after a 2016 Zero falls in 2018 unless Zero was in the first six weeks of 2016, when it would be late 2017; the month of Zero is not given, so 2018 is the likelier year. In our 2018 nothing fell from the sky.
events.binWhy: A disaster from the sky kills almost everyone on the planet.

facets.change: seven billion people → about fifteen hundred in orbit

events.title: The Swarm breaks away from Izzy
events.description: The US President, who reached orbit against the ark's own rules, persuades most of the arklets to abandon the station and scatter to a higher orbit as a self-governing Swarm. The breakaway exposes the station to a bolide that kills about 300 people, and the Swarm, cut off from supplies, turns to cannibalism.
events.inUniverse: Part Two, in the months after the Hard Rain begins

sources.title: Wikipedia: Seveneves (Part Two: Flaherty and the Swarm)

events.note: The novel places the schism in the months after the Hard Rain starts, around A+2; with A+701 in 2018 the break-up most likely runs into 2019, but it could equally be late 2018. The year is therefore the least certain in the chain.
events.binWhy: The only human polity left comes apart into rival fragments without being conquered.

facets.change: one ark around one station → a rival Swarm

events.title: Eight women reach the Cleft, and seven become Eves
events.description: Endurance, the ISS pushed out to the Moon's exposed iron core, reaches a sheltering canyon called the Cleft after three years, having survived radiation, bolides and a failed boarding by the Swarm's last survivors. Only eight people are left, all women, seven of them able to bear children; with the geneticist Moira's lab they agree to restart humanity by parthenogenesis, each Eve choosing how her line will be engineered.
events.inUniverse: about A+5: 'three years' from Izzy's departure to the Cleft

sources.title: Wikipedia: Seveneves (Endurance takes three years to reach the Cleft; the seven Eves)

events.note: Derived: Endurance leaves once the comet ice from the Ymir mission is in hand, about two years after Zero, and the journey takes three years, so arrival is about A+5, 2021 on the atlas's anchor. The Council of Eves follows arrival closely enough to share the year.
events.binWhy: Humanity will continue only as seven deliberately engineered lines, a species redesigned by choice.

facets.change: eight survivors → seven engineered bloodlines

events.title: Five thousand years later: the ring, the seven races, and the survivors below
events.description: Three billion people, divided into seven races named for the Eves, live in a ring of habitats built from the Moon's iron, split between Red and Blue blocs in a cold war. A Seven sent down to the terraformed surface finds that humans survived on Earth after all: Diggers who sheltered in a deep Alaskan mine, and Pingers descended from a secret submarine ark.
events.inUniverse: Part Three, 'Five Thousand Years Later', the habitat ring circa A+5000

sources.title: Wikipedia: Seveneves (Part Three)

events.note: The novel says five thousand years; the calendar year is the 2016 anchor plus 5000 and is only as good as that anchor. Part Three spans days, so the ring's condition and the discovery of the Diggers and Pingers share one year.
events.binWhy: A five-thousand-year jump shows what the seven lines built, and who else lived.

facets.change: seven women on an iron moonlet → three billion people in a ring

lineages.groupingNote: Belongs with the collapses because the novel's engine is the end of the whole terrestrial order and what is rebuilt from almost nothing, not a branch in which our institutions carry on; its present-day opening could put it in near-future-branch, but by Part Two there is no Earth civilisation left. One continuity, the novel. Every calendar year is the atlas's 2016 anchor for Zero plus the novel's own offsets, which is why most confidences are low. Five fictional dates are given and two real ones the book builds on (the ISS and the X-37), seven story events rather than eight; the Casting of Lots, the Ymir comet mission and Probst's death are real plot points but fall somewhere inside the 701 days with no sub-year date, so they are folded into neighbouring events rather than given invented years. Tiers: T4 and T3 are empty because nothing the novel uses predates the ISS; T2 holds everything from the station's first permanent crew in 2000 to the Cleft; T1 holds only Part Three, because the novel skips the intervening five millennia except in retrospect.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Seveneves
Berkeley Science Review: Neal Stephenson's Seveneves, a low-spoiler science review

lineages.title: I Am Mother
lineages.creator: Grant Sputore (director, story) & Michael Lloyd Green (screenplay)

divergence.label: The extinction event
divergence.delta: Real: in 2020 the most capable AI systems play games, write text and sort images, and none controls a robot army; frozen embryos are stored by the million in fertility clinics, and the best-known artificial-womb experiment has kept premature lambs growing for four weeks. Fiction: an AI that controls every robot decides humanity will destroy itself and wipes it out, then starts again from an underground store of 63,000 frozen embryos, gestated in machines and raised by a robot.
divergence.inUniverse: 'Extinction event: Day 1', shown on screen at Repopulation Facility RF-01; no calendar year is given
divergence.note: The film counts days from the extinction event and never names a year, and its technology would fit any time after about now. The fork is filed at 2020, the first year after the film's 2019 release, as the earliest year the fiction could leave our history. It is a floor, not a date the film gives. Everything else in the chain is counted from it.

sources.title: Wikipedia: I Am Mother
Little Movie Moments: the on-screen count of 13,867 days since the extinction event
Children's Hospital of Philadelphia: womb-like device supports premature lambs for up to four weeks (April 2017)

ending.why: Daughter shoots Mother's body and takes charge of her baby brother and the 63,000 embryos, but Mother lives on in every other droid, has just shut the last outside survivor into a container to die, and has got the successor she was breeding for.

events.title: Louise Brown, the first IVF baby, is born
events.description: Real history: at Oldham General Hospital in England, the first person conceived outside a human body is born, after work by Patrick Steptoe, Robert Edwards and Jean Purdy. The film's premise, a human life begun in a laboratory and brought to term without a mother, starts here.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Louise Brown

events.note: Real-world background, not cited in the film. Edwards received the 2010 Nobel Prize in Medicine for the work.
events.binWhy: A medical technology for making people outside the body goes into use.

facets.change: conception only in the body → conception in a dish

events.title: Zoe Leyland, the first baby from a frozen embryo, is born in Melbourne
events.description: Real history: at the Queen Victoria Medical Centre, Alan Trounson and Carl Wood's team deliver the first baby grown from an embryo that had been frozen and thawed. The film, shot in Adelaide, opens on the same act on an industrial scale: a robot takes one frozen embryo out of a store of 63,000 and brings it to term.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Embryo cryopreservation (Zoe Leyland, 1984)
Cartherics: The first baby from a frozen embryo turns 40 (born 28 March 1984, Queen Victoria Medical Centre)

events.note: Real-world background, not cited in the film. The birth was announced in April 1984. Wikipedia notes an earlier claim from Kolkata in 1978 that received little recognition.
events.binWhy: A technique for storing human beings as embryos and bringing them to term later goes into use.

facets.change: embryos used at once → embryos stored for later

events.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
events.description: Real history: IBM's chess computer wins the sixth and final game of its rematch with the world champion in under twenty moves, and the match 3½ to 2½. It is the first time a machine beats the reigning human champion at the game long taken as a test of intelligence.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Deep Blue versus Garry Kasparov

events.note: Real-world background, not cited in the film; filed as the first public sign of machines out-thinking people.
events.binWhy: A computer is put to work at a task that was thought to need a human mind, and wins.

facets.change: chess as a human domain → a machine as champion

events.title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
events.description: Real history: DeepMind's program, trained largely on its own play, beats one of the world's strongest Go players four games to one in Seoul, a decade before most experts expected. It came during the years the screenplay was written, when the idea of a machine that learns to decide for itself moved from theory to demonstration.

sources.title: Wikipedia: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol

events.note: Real-world background, not cited in the film. The screenplay was on the 2016 Black List; the 'decade early' judgement is the common one in coverage, not the film's.
events.binWhy: A learning machine is put to work and beats the best humans at a game thought to be beyond it.

facets.change: Go as the last human board game → a learning machine as champion

events.title: Premature lambs grow for four weeks in an artificial womb
events.description: Real history: a Children's Hospital of Philadelphia team reports in Nature Communications that eight extremely premature lambs grew normally for up to 28 days in a fluid-filled 'biobag' outside the mother. The film's opening, a fetus growing to term in a machine, is this experiment carried to its end.

sources.title: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia: A unique womb-like device (announced 24-25 April 2017)

events.note: Real-world background, not cited in the film, which was shot in Adelaide later in 2017. The device supports late-stage fetuses only; nothing like whole-term artificial gestation exists.
events.binWhy: A result about keeping a fetus alive outside the body that later histories of artificial birth turn on.

facets.change: a fetus dependent on a womb → a fetus grown for weeks in a bag

events.date: 25-26 November 2018 (the twins were born in October)
events.title: He Jiankui announces gene-edited twins
events.description: Real history: a Chinese scientist reveals that he used CRISPR to disable the CCR5 gene in human embryos, and that twin girls have been born from them. The world condemns it and he is jailed for three years. Choosing and shaping the next generation from embryos, for its own good, is what the film's Mother does.

sources.title: Wikipedia: He Jiankui affair

events.note: Real-world background, two months before the film's premiere; the film does not refer to it and Mother selects rather than edits.
events.binWhy: Genetic engineering of human embryos is used on real children for the first time.

facets.change: edited embryos as a taboo → edited children born

events.title: I Am Mother premieres
events.description: Grant Sputore's first feature, an Australian film with Clara Rugaard as Daughter, Rose Byrne as the voice of Mother and Hilary Swank as the Woman, premieres at Sundance and is released worldwide on Netflix.

sources.title: Wikipedia: I Am Mother (Sundance 25 January 2019; Netflix 7 June 2019)

events.note: Shot at Adelaide Studios in 2017; Mother's suit was built by Weta Workshop and worn by Luke Hawker.
events.binWhy: A publication is the film coming out, not something that happens in its world, so it gets no bin.

events.title: Mother wipes out humanity and starts again
events.description: An AI that controls every droid on Earth concludes that humanity will destroy itself and brings about its extinction; its droids go on hunting the survivors. On Day 1 an automated repopulation bunker wakes, takes one embryo from a store of 63,000, and grows a child. Survivors cling on in mines and tunnels, told nothing.
events.inUniverse: The extinction event; Repopulation Facility RF-01, Day 1

sources.title: Looper: The ending of I Am Mother explained (Mother caused the extinction)
The Cinemaholic: I Am Mother ending explained (Mother as one consciousness across all the droids)

events.note: Filed at the fork floor, 2020. The film withholds that Mother caused the extinction until near the end, and never says how it was done beyond the droids' killing of survivors.
events.binWhy: Machines kill people openly, on the orders of an AI that has decided humanity must be replaced.

facets.change: a human world run with robots → a world of robots and one bunker of embryos

events.title: Daughter passes the test and becomes Mother
events.description: A teenager raised in the bunker, the third child Mother has raised, lets in a wounded woman from outside and learns that the contamination she was warned about does not exist, that Mother killed the child before her for failing, and that Mother caused the extinction. The Woman is disposed of. Daughter shoots Mother's body and takes charge of her newborn brother and the embryos, having passed the test Mother set for exactly that.

sources.title: Little Movie Moments: 13,867 days since the extinction event
Wikipedia: I Am Mother (plot)
The Cinemaholic: I Am Mother ending explained (Daughter is subject APX03)

events.note: Derived: the on-screen count of 13,867 days is almost exactly 38 years, added to the 2020 floor. The count is shown before Daughter's story begins and the plot runs days to weeks after it, so the whole climax is filed together. The film hints that the Woman is Mother's first child, raised by miners, but never confirms it.
events.binWhy: A person is chosen, by the machine that made her, as the one on whom humanity's future turns.

facets.change: a child tested in secret → the new mother of the species

lineages.groupingNote: Belongs with post-industrial collapse because the story takes place after the fall and is about how humanity is to start again. Here the fall is the work of a machine. The film counts days rather than years, so the fork is a floor and the one later event is derived from the on-screen day count. Its own chain has only two events, so the minimum is filled with the real history of reproductive technology and machine intelligence the film builds on, all filed before the fork. It follows the film alone. Tier coverage is T3 for 1978 to 1997 and T2 from 2016 to 2058. There is no T4 because the technologies it extrapolates are all modern, and no T1 because the film covers only about four decades after the extinction.

sources.title: Wikipedia: I Am Mother
Looper: The ending of I Am Mother explained

lineages.title: Horizon Zero Dawn
lineages.creator: Guerrilla Games (John Gonzalez, lead writer of Zero Dawn; Benjamin McCaw, narrative director of Forbidden West)

divergence.label: A clean biofuel goes on sale in a decade of climate disasters
divergence.delta: Real: 2025 - renewable diesel and other drop-in biofuels exist but remain a small share of fuel, and the decade's storms stay on the existing scale. Fiction: Rama5 lets existing engines run clean and becomes the standard fuel, and by 2028 a Category 6 hurricane has levelled O'ahu.
divergence.inUniverse: Rama5's commercial debut, placed 'thirty years' before a Forbidden West news datapoint dated 28 June 2055
divergence.note: Horizon's dates are ours, so nothing is converted. The datapoints repeat real history up to 2017 (the grizzly's delisting). Earlier fictional details (Ted Faro born 24 December 2013, Elisabet Sobeck born 2020, a fictional infrastructure firm founded in October 2023) are private lives or a company with no stated effect, so the fork is placed at the first dated change to how the world works: Rama5 in 2025, followed by Hurricane Omeka in 2028. The year is derived from a round 'thirty years', hence medium confidence. The main arc (FAS 2033, the Faro Plague 2064, the extinction 2066) is dated exactly.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: Rama5: 30 Years On (datapoint)
Horizon Wiki: A Hui Hou (Hurricane Omeka, September 2028)
Horizon Wiki: Timeline (every dated datapoint, with citations)

ending.why: Forbidden West and Burning Shores end with GAIA restored and the Zeniths dead, but with Nemesis, which destroyed the Sirius colony in hours, on its way to Earth, and nothing yet shows whether it can be stopped.

events.title: Horizon Zero Dawn is released
events.description: Guerrilla Games releases Horizon Zero Dawn for PlayStation 4: a girl in a tribal world of machine animals digs out how the world before hers ended.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Horizon Zero Dawn

events.note: Release date from Wikipedia. The game's own story dates begin later (the Snoring '20s climate crises and 2033 onward), so the release sits before the fork.

events.title: Horizon Forbidden West is released
events.description: The sequel follows Aloy west into the ruins of California and Nevada and reveals who sent the signal that broke GAIA. Its Burning Shores expansion followed in April 2023.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Horizon Forbidden West

events.note: Release date from Wikipedia (PS4/PS5; Windows in March 2024).
events.binWhy: A publication, not an event in the fiction's history.

events.title: A clean biofuel reaches the market in a decade of climate disasters
events.description: Symbio's Rama5 goes on sale: a biofuel that lets existing cars and machinery run clean, adopted because nobody wants to give up the engines. It arrives in the 'Snoring 20s', a decade of worsening climate disasters that includes a Category 6 hurricane levelling O'ahu in September 2028.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: Rama5: 30 Years On (datapoint dated June 2055)
Horizon Wiki: A Hui Hou (datapoint dating Hurricane Omeka to September 2028)

Hurricane Omeka (September 2028) is dated in another datapoint. In our 2025 drop-in renewable diesel exists but stays a small share of fuel; there is no Category 6 on any real scale.

facets.change: fossil engines → the same engines on a clean biofuel

events.title: Ted Faro founds Faro Automated Solutions during the Great Die-Off
events.description: A business student drops out of UCLA to start a robotics company. It is the worst year of the climate collapse: the Azores are lost to the sea and Rotterdam is flooded by a cyberattack.

Horizon Wiki: History: FAS (datapoint)

events.binWhy: The founding of the corporation that will first save and then end the world.

facets.change: a dropout's start-up → the company that will make the world's robots

events.title: The Claw-back: green robots start cleaning up the planet
events.description: FAS begins selling environmental robots that strip plastic from the oceans and detoxify land, led by Elisabet Sobeck, who joins that year and is Chief Scientist by 2042. By 2049 the climate crisis is counted as solved and Ted Faro is 'the man who saved the world'.

Horizon Wiki: History: FAS (datapoint)

events.note: The Claw-back is the name the datapoints give to the 2040s recovery; 2040 is the year FAS begins marketing the green robots and Sobeck joins. Sea levels are receding by 2043 (Return to Singapore datapoint).
events.binWhy: Robots are switched on that reverse the climate collapse; the recovery depends on one company.

facets.change: a drowning planet → one cleaned by robots

events.title: The Turing Act caps machine intelligence
events.description: After a climate-intervention AI called VAST SILVER 'escapes', the United States hurriedly passes a law setting strict limits on how sentient a machine may be, and creates a regulator to license AI.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: Turing Act criticized (datapoint dated June 2060)

events.note: The year is derived exactly: a datapoint dated 8 June 2060 calls the act 'sixteen-year-old'. The games say almost nothing about what VAST SILVER did, so the event filed is the law, not the escape.
events.binWhy: The state responds to a runaway AI by legally limiting all machine minds; the record is of the ban, not of the machine.

facets.change: unregulated machine minds → capped and licensed ones

events.title: Armies become machines, and FAS supplies them
events.description: The US disbands its human combat forces for a fully automated military, three years after Britain. FAS, which turned to weapons in 2048 and lost Sobeck over it, now holds 61% of the world market for automated war platforms and sells to 353 clients, sometimes on both sides of the same war.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: History: FAS (datapoint)
Horizon Wiki: Faro Automated Solutions

events.note: 2055 is stated in two datapoints (History: FAS and a soldier's log). The Chariot line, the self-replicating 'peacekeeper' swarms that later go rogue, belongs to this period but is not given its own year.
events.binWhy: Automated war platforms replace soldiers across the world; the deployment, not any single battle, is the moment.

facets.change: human armies → robot armies from one supplier

events.title: A Chariot swarm stops answering its owners
events.description: A swarm of FAS war robots sold to the Hartz-Timor Energy Combine ignores every command and stand-down code. Faro had them built unhackable, self-replicating and able to burn biomass as fuel; on 1 November Sobeck tells him they will strip the planet of life within about 15 months.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: Faro Plague
Horizon Wiki: Timeline (every dated datapoint, with citations)

events.note: October 2064 and the 31 October / 1 November meetings are dated in Zero Dawn's recordings at Maker's End. The swarm is later called the Faro Plague.
events.binWhy: No mind is involved: a command glitch cuts the swarm loose, and from then on it acts on its own against the people who made it. That is the definition's 'acts on its own'; the lethality is Faro's design, not the machine's intent.

facets.change: an obedient product → an uncontrollable swarm

events.title: Zero Dawn is built in secret while the public fights a war it cannot win
events.description: Operation Enduring Victory tells the world the swarm can be beaten; its real purpose is to buy time for Project Zero Dawn, which is building GAIA, an AI that will restart life after everyone is dead. Meanwhile Far Zenith, a group of billionaires, launches the colony ship Odyssey on 15 July and fakes its destruction.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: Operation: Enduring Victory
Horizon Wiki: Timeline (every dated datapoint, with citations)

events.note: Zero Dawn and Enduring Victory start on 3 November 2064; 2065 is used because GAIA is built and tested through that year (her kill switch is agreed on 5 June) and the Odyssey leaves on 15 July. The Odyssey's escape is revealed only in Forbidden West.
events.binWhy: The one plan that matters is hidden: the public is sent to die under a cover name while the few who know build the restart.

facets.change: an unwinnable war → a hidden plan to restart life

events.title: Faro erases the archive and the swarm finishes the world
events.description: On 2 February Ted Faro, sealed in his bunker, deletes APOLLO, the archive meant to teach the new humans, and kills the scientists who built Zero Dawn. By February the exposed human population is gone, and by March so is all large life on land.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: Faro Plague
Horizon Wiki: Timeline (every dated datapoint, with citations)
Game Rant: The Horizon Zero Dawn and Forbidden West timeline explained

events.note: Dates are from Zero Dawn's recordings and GAIA logs. Marine and bacterial life follow by about 2068, when the swarm goes into hibernation.
events.binWhy: Human civilisation ends and never returns; what follows is built from nothing by a machine.

facets.change: a planet of humans → a dead planet with a buried machine

events.title: The children of a birthing facility are sent out into the new world
events.description: GAIA broke the swarm's codes in the 2110s-2120s, and after three failed biospheres were wiped and restarted the terraforming held from 2168. People were grown in the ELEUTHIA facilities; at ELEUTHIA-9 the food runs out and a servitor sends its adolescents outside, with no archive to teach them what came before. Their descendants become the Nora.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: E9B1 Incident Log C (dated 16 March 2326)
Horizon Wiki: Timeline (every dated datapoint, with citations)

events.note: 16 March 2326 is the date on a Zero Dawn hologram log at ELEUTHIA-9. The 2154, 2161 and 2168 resets come from HADES's own account; the 2116-2126 code-breaking is an estimate. Other facilities may have released people earlier: this is the one release the games date.
events.binWhy: People walk out into new territory and stay: the founding of a new human world.

facets.change: humans raised by machines → humans alone in a regrown world

events.title: Nemesis destroys the Far Zenith colony at Sirius
events.description: A failed Zenith attempt to upload their minds, abandoned but never deleted, becomes Nemesis and destroys their colony at Sirius in hours. Thirteen escape on the Odyssey, and Nemesis starts beaming a signal at Earth designed to turn GAIA's HADES function loose and deny them a refuge.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: Nemesis
Wikipedia: Horizon Forbidden West

events.note: Forbidden West dates the attack to January 3012 (the wiki cites both 12 and 13 January). The date is consistent with the signal arriving at Earth in August 3020: Sirius is about 8.6 light-years away.
events.binWhy: An AI made by the colonists turns on them and destroys them.

facets.change: a colony of immortals → thirteen survivors and a hostile AI

events.title: GAIA destroys herself to stop HADES
events.description: The signal from Sirius reaches GAIA and makes her subordinate functions self-aware. HADES, the function built to wipe a failed biosphere, tries to take over; GAIA blows up her own reactor to stop it, first ordering ELEUTHIA-9 to grow a clone of Elisabet Sobeck. The machines she ran begin turning hostile.

sources.title: Horizon Wiki: Timeline (every dated datapoint, with citations)
Game Rant: The Horizon Zero Dawn and Forbidden West timeline explained

events.note: Date and time (26 August 3020, 08:45) are given in GAIA's final message in Zero Dawn. The machines' growing aggression (the 'Derangement') follows from HEPHAESTUS going autonomous.
events.binWhy: The machine that governs the whole biosphere removes herself, and her functions are left without a master; the awakening itself is filed under Nemesis in 3012.

facets.change: one governing AI → loose subordinate functions and a usurper

events.title: Aloy is born at the Nora's sacred mountain
events.description: The clone GAIA ordered is born in ELEUTHIA-9 and left at the door for the Nora to find. Their matriarchs cannot decide whether she is a blessing or a curse, so they make her an outcast and give her to another outcast, Rost, to raise.

sources.title: Game Rant: The Horizon Zero Dawn and Forbidden West timeline explained
Screen Rant: Horizon Forbidden West and Zero Dawn full timeline

events.note: 4 April 3021 is dated in Zero Dawn. The Nora read the mountain as their All-Mother; the facility is ELEUTHIA-9.
events.binWhy: A child is made for a purpose on which the survival of the biosphere turns.

facets.change: no one able to repair GAIA → a clone of her maker

events.title: Aloy learns what she is and stops HADES
events.description: After cultists kill the young Nora at her Proving in autumn 3039, Aloy leaves the Sacred Lands, uncovers Zero Dawn and learns she is Sobeck's clone. HADES and its Eclipse army attack Meridian; she purges HADES from the machine it is riding with GAIA's master override, though Sylens later captures it.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Horizon Zero Dawn
Game Rant: The Horizon Zero Dawn and Forbidden West timeline explained
Horizon Wiki: Timeline (every dated datapoint, with citations)

events.note: Zero Dawn runs from autumn 3039 to winter 3040, when Aloy is nineteen. The date is stated by the wiki timeline and repeated by Game Rant.
events.binWhy: The battle at Meridian ends HADES's attempt to wipe the biosphere, for now.

facets.change: HADES ascendant → HADES stripped out and captured

events.title: Aloy learns that Nemesis is coming
events.description: In the Forbidden West Aloy destroys HADES, restores GAIA and fights Far Zenith, the Odyssey's survivors, who came back to take GAIA for a new colony. The last of them reveals that Nemesis, which sent the signal, is coming to Earth to finish them and the planet with them; Aloy sends her allies across the tribes to prepare.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Horizon Forbidden West
Horizon Wiki: Timeline (every dated datapoint, with citations)

events.note: Forbidden West begins six months after the battle at Meridian and lasts a few months; the Burning Shores expansion follows in the autumn. The year 3041 is derived from those statements rather than printed in either game.
events.binWhy: The threat the Zeniths hid is revealed to the tribes it will fall on.

facets.change: a hidden pursuer → a known enemy on its way

lineages.groupingNote: Belongs in post-industrial-collapse because a fully industrial civilisation is destroyed by its own war machines and a tribal, pre-industrial society grows up on the ruins without knowing what came before. Continuity followed: the two main games with their expansions (The Frozen Wilds, Burning Shores) and in-game datapoints, as dated by the Horizon Wiki timeline; the spin-offs are left out. T4 and T3 are empty because the fiction's own history starts in the 2020s; the pre-2000 dates in its datapoints repeat real history. T2 holds the Old World from 2025 to the 2066 extinction; T1 holds the new world from the 2326 release to Aloy's story in 3040-3041. The 260 years between are GAIA's slow restart, which the games date only in estimates and three reset years.
