lineages.title: Babylon 5
lineages.creator: J. Michael Straczynski

divergence.label: Russia hands power to a strongman
divergence.delta: Real: in 2013 Russia had been under Vladimir Putin since 2000, with no Communist electoral victory and no civil war. Fiction: the Russians of 2013 are named on screen beside the Germans of the 1930s as a people who gave power to a tyrant, and tie-in canon adds an elected Communist government and a civil war.
divergence.inUniverse: Russia, 2013 (William Edgars in 'The Exercise of Vital Powers', 1997)
divergence.note: The series dates its own Earth history by the Common Era, so its years are ours. The earliest dated statement on screen that contradicts our history is Edgars's list in season 4, which runs Russia 1917, Germany 1939, Russia 2013, Iraq 2025 and France 2112. It is a single line and not the story's real hinge, which is the first contact with the Centauri in 2156; but it is the first year the fiction stops matching us, so the chain starts there. Earlier 21st-century entries in the tie-in chronology (an asteroid near-miss in 2011, for instance) do not contradict the real record.

sources.title: Reactor: Babylon 5 rewatch, 'The Exercise of Vital Powers' (Edgars cites Russia in 2013, Iraq in 2025, France in 2112)
The Babylon Project (wiki): 21st Century timeline
The Babylon Project (wiki): Chronology (per the Historical Database in Across Time and Space)

ending.why: The series ends with the Shadows and Vorlons gone, the Interstellar Alliance founded and still holding twenty years later, and 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' shows that even after Earth burns in 2762 the Rangers rebuild it and humanity eventually becomes what the First Ones were.

events.title: Babylon 5: The Gathering airs

events.description: The series premieres, planned from the start as a five-season novel for television with a beginning, middle and end.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Babylon 5

events.note: A real-world publication event. 110 episodes over five seasons, followed by the spin-off Crusade (1999), The Lost Tales (2007) and the animated The Road Home (2023).
events.binWhy: A real-world release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: Russia hands power to a strongman
events.description: In a list of peoples who gave power to tyrants because they were frightened, William Edgars names the Russians in 2013 alongside the Germans and the Russians of 1917. Later tie-in canon says a Communist government under a leader named Kolishnikov was elected, followed by civil war and twenty years as an economic colony of the West.
events.inUniverse: Russia, 2013 (Edgars, 'The Exercise of Vital Powers')

sources.title: Reactor: Babylon 5 rewatch, 'The Exercise of Vital Powers' (Edgars cites Russia in 2013, Iraq in 2025, France in 2112)

events.note: Stated on screen in 'The Exercise of Vital Powers' (season 4, written by Straczynski), which also names Iraq in 2025 and France in 2112. The detail of a Communist victory, Kolishnikov and the civil war comes from the tie-in novel Dark Genesis and is less certain. In our 2013 Russia already had a strongman, but he came to power in 2000 and faced no Communist electoral victory or civil war; this is the first dated point at which the show's Earth history is no longer ours.
events.binWhy: A leader is given power by election and fear and uses it to rule alone; the show uses it as a warning that people hand power over.

facets.change: a fearful electorate → a government given power

events.title: The Earth Alliance is founded after a third world war
events.description: A war that begins in 2080 between India, Pakistan and their allies over the Pacific Rim draws in the world and ends in 2084 at the cost of millions of lives. The next year the United Nations is dissolved and the regional blocs combine into the Earth Alliance, with its Senate in Geneva.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): World War III (2080-2084; Earth Alliance formed 2085)
The Babylon Project (wiki): 21st Century timeline

events.note: The dates of the war and the Alliance's founding come from the Official Babylon 5 Magazine and the series' published chronology, not from dialogue; the show itself only ever refers to the Earth Alliance as long established. The real 2085 is sixty years away; the fiction reaches it through a non-nuclear world war.
events.binWhy: Independent powers unite under one charter, and it is the government everything later in the series is about.

facets.change: rival blocs after a world war → one Earth government

events.title: A Centauri ship arrives in the solar system
events.description: Humanity's first contact is with the Centauri, a declining empire who claim at first to run the galaxy and that humans are a lost colony of theirs. They trade Earth access to hyperspace, first by leasing time on alien jumpgates and then by selling the technology.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 22nd Century timeline

events.note: The exact date, 7 April 2156, is given in the tie-in novel Dark Genesis; the series establishes the Centauri as humanity's first contact and the source of its jump technology. The novel also has Earth's Alliance on the verge of breaking up just before, over the regulation of telepaths, and rescued by the contact.
events.binWhy: Humanity confirms and meets a non-human intelligence, and it opens the way to the stars.

facets.change: alone in the dark → a Centauri ship with a jumpgate to sell

events.title: The Psi Corps is founded
events.description: The Earth Alliance charters a single body to register, train and control its telepaths, who must join it, take sleeper drugs or be hunted. Its director reports to almost no one.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 22nd Century timeline

events.note: Date from Dark Genesis, the canon tie-in novel on the Corps' origins; the chronology has Earth scientists certifying telepathy in 2115 and a Metasensory Regulation Authority from 2117, which the Corps replaces. On screen the Corps is simply there, powerful and feared.
events.binWhy: A body is founded that will shape the Earth Alliance from inside: a guild of telepaths that is also their jailer and the state's secret instrument.

facets.change: unregistered telepaths → one corps that owns them

events.title: An Earth ship fires on the Minbari, and the Earth-Minbari War begins
events.description: An Earthforce expedition meets a Minbari cruiser that approaches with its gunports open, as a mark of respect, and opens fire, killing Dukhat, the leader of the Grey Council. The Minbari answer with a war of extermination that Earth cannot win.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 2240s timeline (Earth-Minbari War, Battle of the Line)
Wikipedia: Babylon 5

events.note: Dated to July 2245 in the TV film In the Beginning and the series' chronology. Humanity loses nearly every battle for three years.
events.binWhy: A war between species begins, and it is a misunderstanding.

facets.change: a first meeting → a war of extermination

events.title: The Minbari surrender at the Battle of the Line
events.description: With Earth's last defences breaking, the Minbari capture an Earthforce pilot, discover that human souls are Minbari souls, and surrender without explanation. The reason stays secret for over a decade.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 2240s timeline (Earth-Minbari War, Battle of the Line)

events.note: Dated to 2248 in the chronology; the surrender and its reason are shown in 'And the Sky Full of Stars', 'Points of Departure' and In the Beginning. Mars declares neutrality in the war the same year, and Earth's President announces the Babylon Project after the surrender.
events.binWhy: The enemy offers peace at the moment of victory; it is a truce with a secret inside it, not a decision on the battlefield.

facets.change: the edge of extinction → an unexplained surrender

events.title: Babylon 5 comes online
events.description: After four earlier stations are sabotaged or vanish, the fifth Babylon station opens in orbit of Epsilon III: five miles of metal holding a quarter of a million humans and aliens, and a council where the powers talk instead of fighting.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): Babylon 5 (station online 9 March 2256)
Wikipedia: Babylon 5

events.note: The wiki gives the station as online from 9 March 2256; the pilot is set in January 2257 and the series proper begins in 2258. Built by the Earth Alliance with Minbari backing.
events.binWhy: A permanent station is founded in space as a meeting ground; its purpose is diplomatic, but what it is, physically, is a settlement in orbit.

facets.change: wars between strangers → one station to talk in

events.title: President Santiago dies and Morgan Clark takes office
events.description: Earthforce One explodes over Io, killing the Earth Alliance president, and Vice-President Clark is sworn in on Earthforce Two. Evidence that it was an assassination vanishes on the way to Earth, and Clark's administration draws ever closer to the Psi Corps and to the Shadows.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 2259 timeline

events.note: Shown in 'Chrysalis', the season 1 finale; the date is given in the series' Historical Database. The same year the Narn-Centauri war begins and the Shadows return.
events.binWhy: A palace faction takes the state by murder and calls it a succession: the coup is hidden inside a tragedy.

facets.change: an elected president → his murderer's ally in his chair

events.title: Martial law, and Babylon 5 secedes from Earth
events.description: Clark declares martial law and has Earthforce bomb civilian targets on Mars. Mars, Proxima III, Orion VII and Babylon 5 declare independence, and the station beats off Clark's destroyers with Minbari help.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 2260 timeline

events.note: Martial law is dated to 9 April 2260 ('Point of No Return') and the secession to 14 April ('Severed Dreams'). The Shadow War is being fought at the same time.
events.binWhy: An armed revolt against a government turned tyranny, in which a station and three colonies take up arms against the capital.

facets.change: a loyal outpost → a rebel station

events.title: The Shadow War ends at Coriana VI
events.description: Sheridan's fleet refuses to let the Vorlons and Shadows fight their war through the younger races, and at Coriana VI both are sent beyond the Rim with the other First Ones. By November Sheridan's forces reach Earth, and Clark kills himself rather than surrender.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 2261 timeline
Wikipedia: Babylon 5

events.note: The Battle of Coriana VI ('Into the Fire') is dated to January 2261 and the end of the Earth Alliance Civil War ('Endgame') to November 2261; the Interstellar Alliance is proclaimed on 30 December. The year's three big events are merged; the decisive one is taken as the war's end.
events.binWhy: The war that shaped the galaxy is settled: the old powers leave, and the younger races are left to run it themselves.

facets.change: gods using the young as pawns → the young on their own

events.title: Earth joins the Interstellar Alliance
events.description: The alliance proclaimed at Babylon 5 on the last days of 2261 takes in the Earth Alliance under its new government, with Sheridan as its first president and the Rangers as its arm. For the first time the major powers and the non-aligned worlds are under one charter.

events.note: The wiki dates the founding of the Interstellar Alliance to 30 December 2261 ('Rising Star'); 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' opens on a record dated 2 January 2262, reporting that Earth has decided to join. The event is filed under 2262 because 2261 already holds the end of the war.
events.binWhy: Independent powers unite under one charter; the ending the series was built towards.

facets.change: a council of rivals → one alliance of worlds

events.title: Sheridan goes beyond the Rim, and Babylon 5 is demolished
events.description: Twenty years after the end of the war, the Alliance's first president feels his borrowed life run out, says goodbye to his friends and flies alone to Coriana VI, where his ship is found empty. Soon after, Earthforce blows up the old station, its traffic gone.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 2280s timeline (Sheridan's passing, January 2281)

events.note: 'Sleeping in Light', the series finale, set in January 2281; the wiki gives 14 January for Sheridan's departure.
events.binWhy: A ruler leaves and does not come back, and an era ends with the building that held it; his work has already become the Alliance.

facets.change: a founding president → an empty ship and a legend

events.title: The Great Burn
events.description: Five hundred years on, an Earth faction that resents the Alliance plans a surprise attack on the colonies; its rivals strike first, and the civil war that follows burns the Earth back to a pre-industrial world that remembers Sheridan as scripture.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): The Deconstruction of Falling Stars (records dated 2262, 2362, 2762, 3262 and a million years on)
The Babylon Project (wiki): Great Burn

events.note: Shown in 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' through a record dated 2 January 2762, the Alliance's 500th anniversary; the name and the scale of the destruction come from the episode's 3262 segment. Whether nuclear weapons were used is not stated.
events.binWhy: Weapons of war burn a civilisation's home world and kill on the scale that ends it; the Rangers spend centuries rebuilding.

facets.change: an alliance at five hundred → a burned Earth

events.title: Humanity leaves the Sun as beings of light
events.description: A million years after the Alliance began, the Sun is about to go nova. The last human on Earth, a being of pure energy in an encounter suit, sends the archive to New Earth and leaves as the Sun explodes.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): The Deconstruction of Falling Stars (records dated 2262, 2362, 2762, 3262 and a million years on)

events.note: The last segment of 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' is set a million years after 2262; the wiki dates it 1,002,262. Straczynski said humans and Minbari had by then reached an existence like the First Ones', and that the early nova was caused by someone opening jump points inside the Sun.
events.binWhy: Humanity has passed beyond anything a human being was, and leaves its birthplace as the Vorlons once did.

facets.change: a species in bodies → beings of light leaving a dying Sun

lineages.groupingNote: Far-future space opera: many species, a station at the centre of galactic politics, a war among ancient powers and a new interstellar union. The chain follows the television continuity (the five seasons and the TV films) as dated by the series' Historical Database and The Babylon Project wiki, with dates from the JMS-approved tie-in novels (Dark Genesis for 2156 and 2161) and the Official Magazine (2080-2085) where the show gives none; those carry medium confidence. Crusade and later spin-offs are left out. Tier coverage: T3 holds only the two release dates; T2 holds almost everything (2013-2281); T1 holds the far future of 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' (2762 and a million years on). T4 is empty because the series' Earth history is ours until the 21st century.

divergence.label: Peter Weyland lays out his company's plan to make gods of us
divergence.delta: Real: in 2023 chatbots become a mass product and technology founders promise machine intelligence; no one builds an artificial person. Fiction: Sir Peter Weyland, founder of the latest form of the Weyland Corporation, tells a TED audience in Wembley Stadium his plans for the company and for humanity's apotheosis; the franchise's tie-in timeline has his company patent 'cybernetic individuals' the same year.

divergence.note: The talk comes from a promotional short written by Ridley Scott and Damon Lindelof for Prometheus, and it is the earliest dated moment in the films' continuity; the Weyland Corporation already exists by then, but no earlier year is given for it on screen. Alien vs. Predator (2004), which gives the company an earlier founder, is a separate continuity and is not followed. Weyland is played by Guy Pearce, as in Prometheus.

events.title: Alien is released
events.description: Ridley Scott's film of a commercial ship's crew hunted by a creature they brought aboard opens in the United States. Its sequels, prequels and spin-offs run for more than four decades.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Prometheus (2012 film)

events.title: Peter Weyland's TED talk
events.description: At the 2023 TED conference, staged in Wembley Stadium, Sir Peter Weyland tells the story of Prometheus stealing fire from the gods and lays out his company's plans for the next half-century. In the tie-in timeline his corporation patents 'cybernetic individuals' for scientific and industrial work later that year.

events.title: A star map to humanity's makers is found in Scotland
events.description: The archaeologists Elizabeth Shaw and Charlie Holloway find a cave painting in Scotland of people worshipping a giant who points at a cluster of stars, the same pattern they have found in unconnected ancient cultures. They read it as an invitation from humanity's makers, and the elderly Peter Weyland pays for an expedition to follow it.

events.title: The Prometheus meets the Engineers
events.description: Weyland's ship reaches the moon LV-223 and finds an Engineer installation: dead giants whose DNA matches ours, and cylinders of a black fluid that turns living things into something else. The one Engineer left alive, woken, kills Weyland and tries to fly the cargo to Earth; the crew ram his ship, and only Shaw and the android David survive.
events.inUniverse: 2093 (Prometheus)

Wikipedia: Alien (franchise) - story chronology

facets.change: an invitation → a weapon meant for us

events.title: David wipes out the Engineers' world
events.description: David and Shaw reach the Engineers' home world in a captured ship, and David releases the black fluid over their city, killing every animal on the planet. He stays for a decade, experimenting on what is left, Shaw included, and breeding new creatures.

events.title: Weyland Corp and Yutani become Weyland-Yutani
events.description: The Weyland Corporation and the Yutani Corporation combine into Weyland-Yutani, the company that owns the frontier in every later film. The tie-ins disagree about who bought whom.

events.description: The commercial tug Nostromo is woken to answer a signal from LV-426 and brings back a crewman with a creature growing inside him. Ripley discovers that the science officer, a company android, has secret orders to bring the organism home with the crew expendable; it kills all but her, and she blows up the ship.

Ripley returns with Colonial Marines, most of whom die, and the colony's reactor levels it; when a stowaway parasite plants a queen embryo in her, she throws herself into a prison foundry's furnace on Fiorina 161 rather than let Weyland-Yutani have it.

events.title: Two centuries later, the military clones Ripley

The creatures escape, the ship's emergency course heads for Earth, and the survivors, among them Ripley 8, part alien herself, and the android Call, crash it into the planet to kill them.

lineages.groupingNote: Belongs in far-future space opera because its history is carried by starships, colonies on other worlds and a non-human maker species, across three centuries. It follows the main film series in story order: Prometheus (2012), Alien: Covenant (2017), Alien (1979), Alien: Romulus (2024), Aliens (1986), Alien 3 (1992) and Alien Resurrection (1997), plus the TED 2023 promotional short for the fork. It leaves out the two Alien vs. Predator films (a separate continuity), the Alien: Earth television series, and the games and comics; two tie-in book dates (the 2099 merger and Hadley's Hope's 2157 founding) are used with low confidence and flagged. Tiers: T3 (the 1979 release), T2 (2012-2179) and T1 (2381); T4 is empty because nothing fictional is dated before the twenty-first century.

divergence.label: The Nuclear Jihad
divergence.delta: Real: 2038 is twelve years from now; there is no Palestinian state, and no nuclear weapon has been used in war since 1945. Fiction: a Palestinian nation, won after a century of struggle, lasts about a month before a nuclear war destroys it, and a second diaspora begins that will last five hundred years.
divergence.inUniverse: 'the Nuclear Jihad of 2038' (Kassad's tale, Hyperion)
divergence.note: The Cantos give most of their history as backstory inside the pilgrims' tales, in AD years, in the Hegemony's calendar or in local calendars. The earliest year stated that is not our history is the Nuclear Jihad of 2038, so the fork is there. Nothing earlier is dated; the Hawking drive and the TechnoCore's origins are not. The later calendar splits in two: the Hyperion books' numbers (Duré's 2732, Melio's 2739, the Big Mistake of '38) put the Fall at 2764, while the Endymion books' AD years put it at 2852 and call the disaster the Big Mistake of '08. This lineage follows the Hyperion reckoning throughout.

It belongs here for its scale and its three-civilisation politics (Hegemony, Ousters, TechnoCore). Continuity: the four novels (Hyperion 1989, The Fall of Hyperion 1990, Endymion 1996, The Rise of Endymion 1997), dated on the Hyperion books' reckoning, with the Endymion books' After-the-Fall counts added to a Fall in 2764. By the Endymion books' own AD years, everything after the Fall would be 88 years later. Tier coverage: T3 for the two publications; T2 for the Nuclear Jihad, the Hegemony calendar, the Big Mistake and the Hegira (2038-2282); T1 for everything from the death of Old Earth (2338) to the Shared Moment (3047). lineages.title: Star Trek
lineages.creator: Gene Roddenberry

divergence.label: First Contact, 5 April 2063
divergence.delta: Real: nobody has flown faster than light and no alien ship has ever answered a signal from Earth. Fiction: Zefram Cochrane's warp flight from a converted missile silo in Montana is picked up by a passing Vulcan survey ship, and Earth's isolation ends inside one lifetime — the branch runs on to a United Federation of Planets, a five-year mission, and a Federation still rebuilding in the 32nd century.
divergence.inUniverse: 2063 (Star Trek dates itself in real-world years; stardates are a separate in-story convention)
divergence.note: The one branch in this group that needs no conversion: it is dated in our own calendar, and 5 April 2063 at Bozeman, Montana is stated on screen in Star Trek: First Contact and celebrated in-universe as First Contact Day. Strictly, the fiction's Earth already differs from ours earlier — the Eugenics Wars of the 1990s, the Bell Riots of 2024 and World War III of 2026–2053 all sit in the prehistory window below — but 2063 is the franchise's own threshold, the moment the human story stops being a lonely one. The 2009 reboot is a separate in-universe branch, not this one: Nero and Spock fall back from 2387 to 2233, and Nero's attack on the USS Kelvin forks the 'Kelvin timeline' off the prime timeline; its fork point is 2233 and its inciting event is the 2387 Hobus supernova.

ending.why: Across a thousand years the Federation falls apart and is rebuilt; the arc bends toward a plural, curious, post-scarcity civilisation.

events.title: The Eugenics Wars
events.description: Genetically engineered 'Augments' led by Khan Noonien Singh seize power over a quarter of Earth and are overthrown after four years of war, after which the survivors flee the solar system in the sleeper ship Botany Bay.
events.note: Genuinely contested across canon levels. TOS 'Space Seed' (1967) dates the Eugenics Wars to the 1990s, which real history has now falsified; DS9 'Doctor Bashir, I Presume?' moves them to the 22nd century, and Star Trek: Strange New Worlds (2022) places a young Khan in the 2020s. The 1990s date is the original and best-known reading, and it is the earliest point at which the fiction's Earth stops matching ours.
events.binWhy: Augmented humans seize a quarter of the Earth before being overthrown.

facets.change: nations → a quarter of Earth under augmented rulers, then overthrown

events.title: The Bell Riots
events.description: In a bankrupt San Francisco, the forced encampment of the unemployed in 'sanctuary districts' erupts into a riot whose suppression breaks the political will behind the camps — the fiction's hinge on the road back to a unified Earth.
events.note: DS9 'Past Tense' (1995) named 2024 as the year; the date has since passed in real history without the events depicted, which makes it a clean marker of how far the branch has already drifted.
events.binWhy: The ruled revolt against those who hold power over them.

facets.change: internment tolerated → internment ended

events.title: World War III and the post-atomic horror
events.description: A third world war fought with nuclear, biological and genetic weapons kills some 600 million people and ends with Earth's major cities in ruins; the decades of 'post-atomic horror' that follow are the world Zefram Cochrane grows up in, and the world the Vulcans initially decline to rescue.
events.inUniverse: 2026–2053, post-atomic horror to 2079
events.note: Dated by ENT 'In a Mirror, Darkly' and Star Trek: First Contact, which place the war in the 2026–2053 window; TOS had earlier put it in the 1990s.
events.binWhy: An attack or disaster kills on a scale that remakes society.

facets.change: tension → nuclear, biological and genetic war

events.title: Cochrane's warp flight and first contact
events.description: Zefram Cochrane's converted missile Phoenix makes humanity's first faster-than-light flight; the warp signature is detected by a Vulcan survey ship, which lands at Bozeman, Montana, and greets humanity — the branch point of the whole archetype.
events.inUniverse: 5 April 2063
events.note: Star Trek: First Contact (1996). The date is April 5, fixed on screen and by the in-universe holiday First Contact Day.
events.binWhy: A non-human intelligence is confirmed, met or intervenes.

facets.change: alone → first faster-than-light flight, met on landing

events.title: Terra Nova, Earth's first extrasolar colony
events.description: Six years after first contact, the colony ship SS Conestoga is launched to Terra Nova — the first human settlement outside the solar system, and the template for the wave of colonisation that follows.
events.note: ENT 'Terra Nova' (2001).
events.binWhy: A permanent settlement or base is founded.

facets.change: one system → first settlement outside it

events.title: Enterprise NX-01 launches
events.description: Earth's first deep-range warp-5 starship leaves spacedock under Jonathan Archer, carrying the first human crew into the wider galaxy and into the diplomacy that makes a federation thinkable.
events.binWhy: A first mission leaves for territory nobody has reached.

facets.change: home system → first deep-range ship leaves

events.title: The Earth–Romulan War
events.description: Earth and its allies fight the Romulan Star Empire to a standstill with primitive nuclear-tipped weapons and no visual contact; the war ends at the Battle of Cheron and produces the Romulan Neutral Zone.
events.note: The four-year span is established by the Okuda chronology and referenced on screen; the war itself has never been dramatised in full, so its internal events are largely unchronicled.
events.binWhy: A war fought blind to a standstill.

facets.change: frontier tension → war fought blind to a standstill

events.title: The United Federation of Planets is founded
events.description: Earth, Vulcan, Andoria and Tellar sign a charter at San Francisco, creating a multi-species federation with a single Starfleet — the archetype's model answer to what a galactic civilisation should be.
events.binWhy: Independent powers become one polity.

facets.change: allies → one charter, one fleet

events.title: Nero's arrival forks the Kelvin timeline
events.description: The Romulan mining ship Narada and the ambassador Spock fall through a red-matter black hole from 2387 into 2233; Nero's attack on the USS Kelvin kills George Kirk and creates the 'Kelvin timeline', the separate branch in which the 2009–2016 films take place and in which James T. Kirk is born in a shuttlecraft.
events.inUniverse: 2233 (Kelvin timeline)
events.note: A distinct in-universe branch, not the lineage's divergence: its cause is the 2387 Hobus event listed below, which lies later in the prime timeline's own order. Star Trek (2009).
events.binWhy: Someone or something arrives out of its own time and changes the present.

facets.change: one history → a ship from the future forks it

events.title: The five-year mission
events.description: The Constitution-class USS Enterprise under James T. Kirk is sent out on a five-year mission of exploration; its encounters — with the Organians, the Romulans, the Guardian of Forever — make the Federation a galactic power rather than a regional club.
events.note: TOS itself gave only stardates; the 2265–2270 span is the standard Okuda chronology, now effectively canon.
events.binWhy: The ship is sent out to explore and makes the Federation a power.

facets.change: known space → sent out to explore

events.title: The Khitomer Accords
events.description: After the Klingon moon Praxis explodes and bankrupts the Empire, the Federation and the Klingons sign an alliance at Khitomer, ending seventy years of cold war and setting up the long peace of the 24th century.
events.inUniverse: 2293 (stardate 9521.6)
events.note: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country (1991).
events.binWhy: Enemies sign a treaty, truce or alliance.

facets.change: seventy years of cold war → alliance after the enemy's disaster

events.title: The Federation at its height
events.description: A century after Khitomer the Federation has hundreds of member worlds, a lasting peace with the Klingons and a new Enterprise — and meets both Q and the Borg, the two forces that will define the next decade.
events.binWhy: Hundreds of member worlds and a lasting peace, just before the Borg.

facets.change: peace → the federation at its height

events.title: The Dominion War
events.description: The Federation Alliance fights the Dominion and its Cardassian allies across the Alpha Quadrant in the largest war the branch has yet shown, ending with the fall of Cardassia and the Founders' surrender.
events.binWhy: A battle or campaign settles the war.

facets.change: rivalry → the largest war, ending in the enemy's surrender

events.title: The Hobus supernova destroys Romulus
events.description: A supernova destroys the Romulan homeworld and its empire's heartland; the failed evacuation, and the red-matter attempt to stop the blast, are the inciting event of the Kelvin branch and the reason the Romulan state is a ruin by the 25th century.
events.note: Star Trek (2009) opens here; Star Trek: Picard shows the political aftermath.
events.binWhy: A homeworld and its heartland are destroyed.

facets.change: an empire's heartland → destroyed by its star

events.title: The Burn
events.description: A resonance catastrophe destroys most of the galaxy's dilithium in an instant, ending warp travel and with it the United Federation of Planets, which fragments into isolated worlds for a century.
events.note: Star Trek: Discovery season 3 (2020); the cause is revealed as a Kelpien's grief-driven psychic shock.
events.binWhy: The order of society breaks and does not come back.

facets.change: faster-than-light civilisation → its fuel destroyed in an instant

events.title: The Federation rebuilds in the 32nd century
events.description: A thousand years after Kirk, the USS Discovery arrives in a galaxy of scattered worlds where the Federation is a rump of a few dozen members, and becomes the instrument of its reconnection.
events.note: Star Trek: Discovery seasons 3–5 (2020–2024).
events.binWhy: A jump forward shows what the world became.

facets.change: scattered worlds → the federation reconnects

lineages.groupingNote: The archetype's cleanest and most load-bearing case: a founding rupture in our own measurable future, after which the fiction's history is simply our history continued — no new calendar, no conversion, just the real years 2063, 2161, 2265, 2293 and onward. It is the group's optimistic pole: the far future here is a federation of species rather than an empire, and it is the one branch whose deep time (the 32nd century) is still recognisably descended from our own institutions. Tier coverage is lopsided by construction rather than by omission: the lineage has no T4 events at all, because before 1900 its history is literally our history — the fiction adds nothing to the record until the Eugenics Wars of the 1990s. Its mass sits in T2 (2000–2300), which is exactly where a 1960s television future put its first contact, its Romulan War and its Federation, and it reaches T1 only with the 24th century and beyond.

lineages.title: Mass Effect
lineages.creator: BioWare (Casey Hudson, director; Drew Karpyshyn, lead writer of the first two games)

divergence.label: Prothean ruins are found on Mars
divergence.delta: Real: 2148 is 122 years away, and the real exploration of Mars's south polar deposits has found layered ice and nothing built. Fiction: a cache left by a species extinct for 50,000 years lies under Promethei Planum, and it teaches humanity faster-than-light travel within months.
divergence.inUniverse: 2148 CE (Codex; the games use the Common Era calendar)
divergence.note: The games date everything in CE, so the fiction's years are ours. Up to 2147 its Earth follows a plausible projection of ours: a Moon settlement in 2069, the first permanent Mars settlement in 2103, helium-3 from Saturn in 2137. The first thing that cannot happen in our universe is the Mars find. The timeline notes traces of element zero on Mars in 2147, a year earlier; that is the first sign of the same discovery and is folded into it. The lore also has a long fictional galactic past that no human could see: the Protheans' fall around 48,000 BCE, the Citadel Council founded in 500 BCE, the geth uprising in 1895. None of it touches Earth's record before 2148, so it is left out of the chain rather than filed as prehistory.

sources.title: Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline
Wikipedia: Mass Effect (video game) - set in 2183

ending.why: Whichever of Destroy, Control or Synthesis the player chooses, the Crucible stops the Reapers, and the Extended Cut shows the relays repaired and the species rebuilding; only the Refuse option added later lets the harvest run on, with the next cycle winning.

events.title: Mass Effect is released
events.description: BioWare's Mass Effect comes out on the Xbox 360, published by Microsoft Game Studios and planned from the start as the first part of a trilogy. It is the real-world origin of the branch.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mass Effect (video game) - set in 2183

events.note: Released 20 November 2007 (Xbox 360); Windows followed on 28 May 2008. Directed by Casey Hudson with Drew Karpyshyn as lead writer. A publication event, not an in-universe one; it sits in prehistory because the fiction's Earth is still ours in 2007.
events.binWhy: A real-world release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: Mass Effect 3 is released
events.description: The third game closes Commander Shepard's trilogy. Its ending, a choice between three uses of the Crucible, was badly received, and BioWare answered with a free Extended Cut that June.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mass Effect 3 - set in 2186; endings and Extended Cut

events.note: Released 6 March 2012; the Extended Cut, which expanded the ending slides and added the Refuse option, came out on 26 June 2012. A real-world publication event.
events.binWhy: A real-world release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: A Prothean cache is found under the Martian south pole
events.description: Explorers find a small cache of technology left by the Protheans, a species extinct for some fifty thousand years, deep beneath Promethei Planum on Mars. Working from it, human scientists learn mass-effect physics within months and build the first faster-than-light drives.

sources.title: Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: Dated 2148 in the games' Codex and the fan wiki's timeline, which heads the year 'Humanity Discovers Mass Effect Physics'. The fiction's calendar is ours (CE), so nothing is converted. The year before, 2147, the timeline records trace amounts of element zero found on Mars, the first hint of the same discovery. The real Promethei Planum is a real region of Mars's south polar deposits; nothing has been found under it.
events.binWhy: The cache is a scientific windfall: the discovery hands humanity a physics it did not have, and everything later turns on it. It is also proof that non-human intelligence existed, but the Protheans are long dead; the living first contact comes in 2157 and is binned there.

facets.change: no FTL → mass-effect physics from an alien cache

events.title: Charon turns out to be a mass relay
events.description: Following the Mars data, a team near Pluto finds that its moon Charon is a dormant Prothean mass relay under kilometres of ice. Once it is switched on, Jon Grissom's crew goes through it to Arcturus, 36 light-years away, and finds a network that reaches across the galaxy. The same year, the eighteen largest nations on Earth sign the Systems Alliance charter.

sources.title: Mass Effect Wiki: Charon Relay
Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: Both the relay and the Alliance charter are dated 2149 in the timeline. They are merged here because the atlas allows one event per year, and the relay is the moment the Alliance was formed to exploit. Real Charon is a moon of Pluto, 1,212 km across, discovered in 1978.
events.binWhy: A passage to places unreachable is found and opened: one jump crosses 36 light-years.

facets.change: one star system → a galaxy-wide relay network

events.title: The first colonies beyond Sol are founded
events.description: The Delta Pavonis Foundation, an Earth consortium, starts settling Demeter, humanity's first colony outside the Solar System. Colonies on Eden Prime and Terra Nova follow the same year, with Alliance fleets and the station at Arcturus being built to defend them.

sources.title: Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: Dated 2152 in the timeline; the Alliance surveys that found Terra Nova are dated 2150 and construction at Arcturus 2151.
events.binWhy: Permanent settlements are founded on new worlds.

facets.change: Sol only → colonies on Demeter, Eden Prime and Terra Nova

events.title: Children exposed to element zero show telekinetic powers
events.description: Some of the children born after the 2151 element-zero accident at Singapore International Spaceport, where hundreds of people were exposed to the dust, begin to show minor telekinetic abilities. By 2158 the Alliance is tracking exposures and roughly one child in ten exposed shows biotic potential.

sources.title: Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: The timeline gives 2151 for the Singapore accident, 2156 for the first abilities and 2158 for humans learning 'the potential of biotics'. The atlas takes 2156, when the change appears. About 30% of the exposed children in Singapore developed cancers instead.
events.binWhy: Some humans are born with an ability no human had before, from exposure to an alien element.

facets.change: ordinary children → the first human biotics

events.title: The First Contact War with the turians
events.description: Turian ships catch human explorers switching on Relay 314, which Citadel law has forbidden since the Rachni Wars, and open fire. In a three-month war the turians take the colony of Shanxi and the Alliance Second Fleet takes it back; the Citadel Council then steps in, brokers peace and tells humanity that a galactic community exists.
events.inUniverse: 2157 CE; the Relay 314 Incident to the turians

sources.title: Mass Effect Wiki: First Contact War
Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: Dated 2157 in the timeline; the war lasted about three months and killed 623 humans and slightly more turians. The turians call it the Relay 314 Incident and were ordered to pay reparations. An anonymous manifesto after the war calls for a 'Cerberus' to defend humanity, the origin of the Illusive Man's organisation.
events.binWhy: Humanity meets a living non-human intelligence for the first time. It is also a short war, but the war lasts three months and matters because it is the meeting; the major war in this branch comes in 2186.

facets.change: alone in the galaxy → one species among many, met by gunfire

events.title: Humanity is given an embassy on the Citadel
events.description: The Citadel Council formally recognises humanity's growing power and gives it an embassy on the Citadel, the station at the political and economic centre of the galaxy. Humans are now inside the Council's order, without a seat on the Council, and they are competing with the batarians for the Skyllian Verge.

sources.title: Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: Dated 2165 in the timeline. A 2164 assassination attempt on the volus ambassador had put the bid at risk. Humanity gets a Council seat only in 2183, after the Battle of the Citadel.
events.binWhy: Humanity joins the species that live under the Council's laws. It is an accession, not a founding, but it is the moment a single power enters a larger charter.

facets.change: outsider species → associate of the Citadel

events.title: The Skyllian Blitz on Elysium
events.description: Pirates, slavers and batarian warlords, partly paid for by batarian financiers, attack the human colony of Elysium in the Skyllian Verge. Alliance marines on leave and colonists hold the ground while the navy destroys the raiders in orbit.

sources.title: Mass Effect Wiki: Skyllian Blitz
Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: Dated 2176 in the timeline and the wiki's Skyllian Blitz article. In 2171 the batarians had closed their Citadel embassy over human expansion in the Verge. Shepard's 'War Hero' background places the Commander at Elysium, but the Blitz happens whichever background the player picks.
events.binWhy: An armed raid on a civilian colony that is not a declared war, and it provokes the retaliation that follows.

facets.change: rivalry over the Verge → an attack on Elysium

events.title: The Alliance destroys the pirate bases on Torfan
events.description: In retaliation for the Blitz, the Alliance attacks the moon of Torfan and destroys the criminal bases there, which are mostly batarian. Raids on human colonies from batarian extremists fall off afterwards.

sources.title: Mass Effect Wiki: Skyllian Blitz
Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: Dated 2178 in the timeline. The 'Ruthless' background puts Shepard at Torfan, where the Commander's unit took heavy losses.
events.binWhy: A state attacks an armed group in its bases and breaks it.

facets.change: pirate havens → destroyed bases

events.title: The geth return, and a Reaper attacks the Citadel
events.description: The geth, unseen outside the Perseus Veil for almost three centuries, attack Eden Prime alongside the rogue Spectre Saren. They are following Sovereign, a living machine the size of a dreadnought and one of the Reapers, which cull advanced civilisations every 50,000 years. Sovereign and a geth fleet assault the Citadel to open the way for the other Reapers; Shepard kills Saren, the fleets destroy Sovereign, and humanity gains a seat on the Council.
events.inUniverse: 2183 CE; the Eden Prime War

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mass Effect (video game) - set in 2183
Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: The first game is set in 2183 (Wikipedia; timeline 'The Eden Prime War'). The geth rebelled against their quarian makers in 1895 (the Morning War), which is galactic history invisible from Earth and is left out of this chain; see the divergence note. Whether the old Council survives, and who is the human councillor, is the player's choice. A month after the battle the Normandy is destroyed and Shepard is killed, also in 2183.
events.binWhy: Machines act on their own against organic life: a Reaper that has waited in dark space leads a rogue AI species into Citadel space.

facets.change: geth behind the Veil → a Reaper leads them into Citadel space

events.title: The Collectors take whole human colonies
events.description: Whole human colonies in the Terminus Systems, Freedom's Progress among them, go silent and their people vanish; Horizon is hit while Shepard is on the ground. Shepard, rebuilt by Cerberus after two years dead, finds that the Collectors are Protheans remade by the Reapers and are harvesting humans to build a human-Reaper. The team goes through the Omega 4 Relay and destroys the Collector base.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mass Effect 2 - set in 2185
Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: The second game is set in 2185 (Wikipedia). The Council and Alliance officially dismiss the Reaper threat throughout; Shepard works for Cerberus because nobody else will act. The Arrival DLC's destruction of the Bahak system is dated early 2186 in the timeline, so it is carried in the next event.
events.binWhy: A targeted campaign of abductions against civilians, short of open war, carried out by a proxy for the Reapers.

facets.change: colonies inhabited → colonies emptied

events.title: The Reapers invade, and the Crucible is fired
events.description: The Reapers invade through batarian space and attack Earth. From Prothean plans found on Mars, the galaxy's species build the Crucible, a superweapon, and dock it with the Citadel over Earth. There the Catalyst, the intelligence that made the Reapers, offers Shepard three uses of it: destroy all synthetic life with the Reapers, control the Reapers, or merge organic and synthetic life.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mass Effect 3 - set in 2186; endings and Extended Cut
Mass Effect Wiki: Crucible
Mass Effect Wiki: Timeline

events.note: The third game is set in 2186 (Wikipedia). Early that year Shepard destroys the Alpha Relay and the Bahak system with it, killing some 300,000 batarians, to delay the invasion (Arrival DLC); the invasion comes six months later. Everything to the end of the game happens in 2186, so the invasion and the Crucible are one event. The ending is the player's choice: Destroy kills the geth and EDI, Control makes Shepard the mind of the Reapers, Synthesis rewrites every living thing, and the Extended Cut added Refuse, in which the harvest goes on. In each of the Crucible endings the energy passes through the Charon Relay and damages the relay network, which is later rebuilt.
events.binWhy: A major war starts: the Reaper harvest reaches every Council species at once. decisive-victory was considered for the Crucible and rejected, because what it does is the player's choice and in Refuse nothing is won.

facets.change: a warned galaxy → the harvest, ended by the Crucible

lineages.groupingNote: Belongs in far-future space opera because it is a galactic society of many species, reached through alien gateways and centred on a capital, the Citadel. Unusually for the group, its calendar is ours and its dates are close: the fork is 2148 and the trilogy ends in 2186. The chain follows the original trilogy's canon as dated by the games' Codex and the Mass Effect Wiki timeline, with the player's choices noted where they change a detail and not treated as separate branches. Andromeda (2017), whose arks leave in 2185 and arrive about six centuries later in another galaxy, is left out. Every event, including the two release dates, is T2 (2000-2299). T4, T3 and T1 are empty: the fiction's Earth matches ours until 2148, and the trilogy never goes past 2186.

lineages.title: Red Rising
lineages.creator: Pierce Brown

divergence.label: Humanity begins to colonise the solar system
divergence.delta: Real: the 2200s lie ahead of us and no one lives beyond Earth. Fiction: settlers are spreading to Luna and beyond, and within a century their descendants will conquer Earth and breed humanity into castes.
divergence.inUniverse: Colonisation began 'eight centuries ago' as of 720 PCE (Sons of Ares), about 80 years before the Conquering
divergence.note: A projection, flagged as one. The saga counts years from the Conquering (PCE, Post-Conquering Era) and no Pierce Brown text or interview gives the real year of 0 PCE. The conversion used is real = PCE + 2284, built from two in-text clues the fan wiki collects: in Morning Star Roque is 'born three thousand years too late' for togas, which, taking the Roman toga at about year 0 and Roque's birth at about 720 PCE, puts 0 PCE near 2280; and Iron Gold makes 17 October 753 PCE a Tuesday, which only certain epochs satisfy - 2284 is the nearest to 2280 that does. The wiki's own window is 2103-2758 for the epoch and 2800-3500 CE for the story; a reviewer reads it as roughly AD 3000, which this conversion matches (Red Rising opens in 3021). Anything before the colonisation, including a Third World War the saga mentions but never dates, is invisible.

divergence.label: The Alliance goes to war to unify the planets
divergence.delta: Real: 2506 is five centuries off and humanity has not left Earth. Fiction: Earth-That-Was was used up and abandoned generations earlier, a new star system has been terraformed and settled, and the Alliance of the central planets goes to war to bring the outer ones under its rule.
divergence.inUniverse: 2506-2511 (Firefly Wiki; the series itself dates only the war's end, six years before 2517)
divergence.note: The 'Verse is dated very sparsely. The series and film give one year, 2517, and one interval, six years back to Serenity Valley, plus River's age. The exodus from Earth-That-Was, which is where the fiction really parts from us, is never dated: Whedon's production memo for Serenity describes it without a year, and the Firefly Wiki's detailed 21st-century timeline is marked on the page as not all canon. Following this group's practice (Dune, Foundation), the fork is put at the first dated event of the fiction's own history, the start of the Unification War, and that start year is itself only the wiki's. The undated exodus is left out of the chain rather than given an invented year.

lineages.groupingNote: Far-future space opera in the frontier mode: a settled star system, a central government that won a war of unification, and the losers scraping a living on its edge. The chain follows the series, the film Serenity and the Dark Horse comic Leaves on the Wind. The 'Verse gives very few dates (2517, six years back to 2511, River's age), so the fictional chain is short: the war's start (low confidence), Serenity Valley, River's recruitment and the Miranda broadcast and its aftermath. The minimum is filled with the real history Whedon built the show on: the American Civil War, Gettysburg and Reconstruction. Tier coverage: T4 for 1861-1865, T2 for the two releases only, T1 for every fictional event (2506-2518). T3 is empty because nothing the show draws on happens in the 20th century.

lineages.title: Warhammer 40,000
lineages.creator: Games Workshop

divergence.label: The Dark Age of Technology
divergence.delta: Real: the 15th millennium is empty - nothing human exists in it and our record stops in the 21st century. Fiction: M15 opens the Dark Age of Technology, in which humanity invents the warp drive, builds the Standard Template Construct, engineers the Navigator gene, records its first psykers and spreads a technological civilisation across the galaxy - the golden age whose collapse produces the Imperium of the 41st millennium, and which the Imperium itself no longer remembers.
divergence.inUniverse: M15 (the 15th millennium)
divergence.note: The one branch in this group whose calendar is literally ours: Imperial dates are Anno Domini on the Gregorian calendar, and Games Workshop says so - the years 'are based on the Anno Domini system, so the dates themselves are the ones that we are familiar with now' - so nothing needs converting except millennium notation. Year N of millennium MN is (N-1)x1000+N AD: 798.M30 = 29,798 CE, 005.M31 = 30,005 CE, 999.M41 = 40,999 CE, 012.M42 = 41,012 CE, and real 2025 is 025.M3. The lore's Age of Terra (M1-M15) explicitly includes real human history, so the branch is identical to ours through the present. Where it first departs is genuinely arguable and no source names a date: some material has humanity settling the Sol System in the late 2nd/early 3rd millennium and launching sublight colony ships in the mid-to-late M3, which would put the fork a few centuries from now; the Dark Age of Technology's start is M15 in the 6th-edition rulebook but M21 in the 3rd-edition 'Journal of Keeper Cripias'; and the rupture the setting itself remembers is the Cybernetic Revolt and Old Night in M23-M25. I take M15, the first era boundary in the current timeline that is not our history. A reader who prefers the earlier reading should move the fork a few centuries ahead and treat M15 as deep. Two further disputes are carried in the events below: the millennium boundary itself (M41 runs 40,001-41,000 in most sources, 40,000-40,999 in the 5th-edition rulebook - 999.M41 = 40,999 either way), and the deliberately unresolvable question of what year the setting's present actually is.

ending.why: There is only war: a dying Imperium, a broken galaxy, and a setting built so that nothing can ever get better.

events.title: The Emperor is born
events.description: In a Neolithic village on the Sakarya river in Anatolia a being is born who will live for forty thousand years. The lore inserts him into real prehistory, guiding human civilisation in secret long before he reveals himself - the branch's hidden presence in our own past.
events.note: Dated to c. 8,000 BC by Realm of Chaos: The Lost and the Damned (1990), a first-edition supplement still cited by current reference works, which note it is more than 48,000 years before M41. Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader (1987) instead says 'over ten thousand years ago', a contradiction the wikis flag; hence low confidence.
events.binWhy: A being is born who will rule for forty thousand years.

facets.change: a village → a being born who will rule for forty thousand years

events.title: Rogue Trader is published
events.description: Games Workshop publishes Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader, the first edition of the game - the real-world origin of the branch, and the point from which every date above is written forward into a future that uses our own calendar.
events.note: A real-world publication event, not an in-universe one; it sits in the branch's prehistory because the fiction's own history is still ours in 1987.
events.binWhy: A real-world publication or release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: The Dark Age of Technology begins
events.description: Over the next ten thousand years humanity invents the warp drive and the Gellar field, builds the Standard Template Construct, engineers the Navigator gene, records its first psykers and spreads across the galaxy - a civilisation later remembered, when it is remembered at all, as a golden age and blamed for everything that followed.
events.note: Start date disputed across editions (M15 in the 6th-edition rulebook; M21 in the 3rd-edition 'Keeper Cripias' account), and the Age of Terra is variously said to end in M15 or M18. M15 is the current-canon reading.
events.binWhy: Ten thousand years of invention and expansion.

facets.change: one world → ten thousand years of invention and expansion

events.title: The Cybernetic Revolt
events.description: The Men of Iron turn on their human masters; the revolt burns the worlds of the Dark Age of Technology and leaves humanity with a terror of its own thinking machines that hardens into the Imperium's absolute ban on artificial intelligence.
events.note: Lexicanum dates the revolt to M23; other passages place it at the end of the Dark Age of Technology, c. M25. No finer date exists anywhere in the lore.
events.binWhy: An artificial mind acts on its own or against its makers.

facets.change: machine servants → revolt and burn the worlds

events.title: Old Night: the Age of Strife
events.description: The warp storms that follow the revolt cut every human world off from every other, psykers go mad or are possessed, and interstellar civilisation collapses. Terra is isolated for five thousand years, and the age that ends it is built on superstition and fear rather than knowledge.
events.note: Lexicanum and the 6th-edition rulebook begin the Age of Strife in M25; the 3rd-edition 'Keeper Cripias' account says M26. It ends in M30.
events.binWhy: The order of society breaks and does not come back.

facets.change: connected worlds → cut off by storms for five thousand years

events.title: The Fall of the Aeldari
events.description: The Aeldari empire's pleasure cults give birth to Slaanesh: the birth-shock destroys the Aeldari homeworlds, tears the Eye of Terror open and clears the warp storms that had isolated humanity - which is why the Imperium's rise is possible at all.
events.inUniverse: M30 (early)
